meetings.title: Durham City Council Meeting May 19, 2025 (with closed captioning)
meetings.executive_summary: With all seven members present, the Durham City Council adopted the consent agenda 7-0, approved a Legal Aid of North Carolina contract 6-0 with Council Member Chelsea Cook recused, approved conveying surplus skate park amenities to The Scrap Exchange 7-0, and unanimously passed a resolution opposing North Carolina House Bill 765's preemption of local zoning authority. City Manager Bo Ferguson formally presented the $722 million FY 2025-26 proposed budget and $537.6 million CIP following public comment on park lead soil and infrastructure needs. Council then approved the Danube Lane Townhouses rezoning (7-0) and annexation/utility agreement (6-1, Baker voting No over non-contiguous 'doughnut hole' slivers) and unanimously approved the 408-unit Brier Creek Multifamily rezoning spanning the Durham-Wake county line (7-0).

agenda_items.title: Roll Call, National Public Works Week Proclamation, Consent Agenda, and Pulled Items 4 & 18
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Mayor Leonardo Williams called the meeting to order with all seven council members present and presented a National Public Works Week proclamation. Council adopted the consent agenda 7-0 excluding Items 4 and 18, approved Item 4 (Legal Aid of North Carolina) 6-0 with Council Member Cook recusing herself, and approved Item 18 conveying modular skate park ramps from the Wheels property to The Scrap Exchange 7-0 after public support from Mike Johnston of Manifest Skate Shop.

agenda_items.title: Resolution in Opposition to NC House Bill 765
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Mayor Leonardo Williams and Council Member Carl Rist introduced a resolution joining North Carolina municipalities across party lines to oppose House Bill 765 ('An Act to Reform Local Government Development Regulations'), arguing Durham already leads the state on middle-housing reforms via EHC and SCAD while HB 765 undermines local planning authority and Section 160D protections.

agenda_items.title: FY 2025-26 Proposed Budget and FY 2026-31 Capital Improvement Plan Presentation
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Public speakers urged faster park lead soil remediation (Mary Fontana, Molly Flow), funding for neighborhood improvements, and Vision Zero pedestrian infrastructure (Chris Perilstein), alongside comments from Gregory Williams and Sarah DeMotto. City Manager Bo Ferguson then formally presented the $722 million proposed FY 2025-26 budget and 43.71-cent tax rate, drawing initial feedback from all seven council members.

agenda_items.title: Consolidated Annexation – Danube Lane Townhouses (3824 & 3910 Danube Lane)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Planning staff Peyton Burgess and Aaron Cain presented a 5.04-acre request from Brightside Ventures LLC (represented by Laura Holloman of McAdams) to annex and rezone two parcels from RS-20 to PDR 7.813 for up to 30 townhomes or duplexes, including a $10,000 Affordable Housing Fund proffer. Council questioned Durham Public Schools' zero-student generation estimate for townhomes and debated non-contiguous 'doughnut hole' parcels and trail connectivity before approving annexation 6-1 (Baker No) and rezoning/consistency 7-0.

agenda_items.title: Zoning Map Change – Brier Creek Multifamily (Andrews Chapel Road / Cozart Road)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Applicant Worth Mills (Monts Ridge LLC) presented a 16.56-acre rezoning from RR and RS-10 to PDR 25.000 near the Wake County line for up to 408 units (383 apartments and 25 townhomes), proffering 5% of units at 80% AMI for 30 years, $50,000 to the Dedicated Affordable Housing Fund, $16,500 to DPS, and 100% native plantings. While Council Member Baker critiqued peripheral car-centric growth and Council Member Freeman questioned YIMBY advocacy framing by speaker Andy Lowe, Council approved all three motions unanimously 7-0.

votes.item_title: Item 4: Agreement with Legal Aid of North Carolina
votes.notes: Chelsea Cook recused herself (no objection to recusal). Mayor Williams experienced a brief button issue at 00:42:32 resolved with Clerk.
votes.discussion_detail: Item 4, an agreement with Legal Aid of North Carolina (continuing eviction/expunction/restoration legal support reviewed at the May 8 work session), was pulled from consent to allow Council Member Chelsea Cook to recuse herself due to her affiliation. Hearing no objection to her recusal request, the remaining six council members voted unanimously 6-0 to approve the contract. Mayor Williams briefly verified his electronic voting button with the Clerk immediately afterward to ensure his Aye vote was properly recorded.

votes.item_title: Item 18: Resolution Approving Conveyance of Skate Park Amenities to The Scrap Exchange, Inc.
votes.notes: Conveyance pursuant to N.C.G.S. 160A-280; equipment acquired from Wheels property to be kept free and open to the public.
votes.discussion_detail: Item 18 was pulled for public comment by local skate shop owner Mike Johnston (Manifest Skate Shop), who praised the partnership between Durham Parks and Recreation and The Scrap Exchange to repurpose surplus modular skate ramps from the former Wheels property into a free, public community skate park in The Scrap Exchange's oversized Lakewood parking lot. Staff had previously confirmed at the May 8 work session that the conveyance under N.C.G.S. 160A-280 requires free public accessibility. On a motion and second, Council unanimously approved the conveyance 7-0.

votes.item_title: Item 27: Resolution in Opposition to NC House Bill 765
votes.notes: Resolution opposing state preemption bill 'An Act to Reform Local Government Development Regulations'.
votes.discussion_detail: Mayor Williams moved Item 27 forward on the agenda and credited Council Member Carl Rist for first bringing House Bill 765 to Council's attention, explaining that the bill threatens municipal land-use authority and Section 160D protections across North Carolina. Council members noted Durham had already adopted middle-housing and parking reforms proactively via SCAD and EHC, making state preemption punitive rather than helpful. Following a motion and second, the resolution passed unanimously 7-0.

votes.item_title: Item 25: Annexation Ordinance and Utility Extension Agreement – Danube Lane Townhouses
votes.notes: UEA with Brightside Ventures, LLC for 3824 & 3910 Danube Lane (5.04 acres). Baker opposed non-contiguous 'doughnut hole' slivers.
votes.discussion_detail: Planning staff presented the 5.04-acre consolidated annexation for up to 30 townhomes or duplexes along Danube Lane near US 15-501, noting Planning Commission recommended approval 12-0 and the applicant proffered $10,000 to the Dedicated Affordable Housing Fund. During questioning, Council Member Cook challenged Durham Public Schools' model projecting zero new students from 30 townhomes, while Council Member Baker objected to creating unannexed 'doughnut hole' county slivers and lacking full greenway construction on the trail easement. Baker voted No on the annexation and utility extension agreement, which passed 6-1.

votes.item_title: Item 25: UDO Zoning Map Change Ordinance (RS-20 County to PDR 7.813 City) – Danube Lane Townhouses
votes.notes: Authorizes up to 30 townhouse/duplex units with $10,000 Affordable Housing Fund proffer.
votes.discussion_detail: Immediately following approval of the annexation, Council voted on the companion UDO Zoning Map Change converting 3824 and 3910 Danube Lane from RS-20 County to Planned Density Residential (PDR 7.813) City jurisdiction. Council members noted the missing-middle infill townhome scale fit the surrounding corridor near existing transit and commercial nodes. Despite voting against the annexation mechanism, Council Member Baker joined his colleagues in supporting the zoning density, passing the ordinance unanimously 7-0.

votes.item_title: Item 25: Consistency Statement (N.C.G.S. 160D-605) – Danube Lane Townhouses
votes.notes: Statutory consistency finding with the Comprehensive Plan.
votes.discussion_detail: As required under North Carolina General Statutes Section 160D-605, Council considered the formal consistency statement affirming the Danube Lane PDR 7.813 rezoning aligns with Durham's Comprehensive Plan Place Type map. No additional debate occurred on the statutory finding. On a motion and second, the consistency statement was adopted unanimously 7-0.

votes.item_title: Item 26: UDO Zoning Map Change Ordinance (RR & RS-10 to PDR 25.000) – Brier Creek Multifamily
votes.notes: 16.56 acres south of Andrews Chapel Rd / east of Cozart Rd; up to 408 units (383 MF, 25 TH); 5% at 80% AMI for 30 yrs; $50k housing fund; $16.5k DPS.
votes.discussion_detail: Applicant attorney Worth Mills presented the 16.56-acre Brier Creek Multifamily project straddling the Durham-Wake boundary, highlighting proffers of 5% units at 80% AMI for 30 years, $50,000 for the Dedicated Affordable Housing Fund, $16,500 for DPS, 100% native plantings, and full street/sidewalk connectivity coordinated with Raleigh. Council Member Baker critiqued the surrounding car-dependent suburban sprawl pattern while acknowledging infill proximity to existing Brier Creek amenities, and Council Member Freeman criticized pro-development speaker Andy Lowe (Center for New Liberalism) while urging deeper partnerships with Durham affordable housing providers. After Caballero, Middleton, Rist, and Williams praised the developer's responsiveness and added housing supply, Council approved the rezoning unanimously 7-0.

votes.item_title: Item 26: Utility Extension Agreement with Monts Ridge LLC – Brier Creek Multifamily
votes.notes: Authorizes City Manager to enter into UEA with Monts Ridge LLC (site already inside city jurisdiction).
votes.discussion_detail: Following the zoning map approval for Brier Creek Multifamily, Council considered the companion motion authorizing the City Manager to execute a Utility Extension Agreement with Monts Ridge LLC to serve the 408-unit development. Because the Durham portion of the site was already within municipal limits, no annexation vote was required. Council approved the utility extension agreement unanimously 7-0.

votes.item_title: Item 26: Consistency Statement (N.C.G.S. 160D-605) – Brier Creek Multifamily
votes.notes: Statutory consistency finding under N.C.G.S. 160D-605; meeting adjourned immediately after at 10:12 PM.
votes.discussion_detail: To finalize the Brier Creek Multifamily rezoning, Council voted on the statutory consistency statement under N.C.G.S. 160D-605 confirming the PDR 25.000 zoning aligns with Durham's Comprehensive Plan. No additional questions were raised following the earlier project discussion. The consistency statement passed unanimously 7-0, and Mayor Williams adjourned the meeting at 10:12 PM.

disagreements.meeting_title: Durham City Council Meeting May 19, 2025 (with closed captioning)
disagreements.issue: Non-Contiguous 'Doughnut Hole' Slivers and Trail Connectivity on Danube Lane Townhouses (Item 25)
disagreements.summary: Council Member Baker opposed annexing the 5.04-acre Danube Lane parcel due to unannexed county slivers and incomplete greenway construction, while six colleagues supported the project as compatible missing-middle housing.
disagreements.side_a_position: Oppose the annexation/UEA creating unannexed 'doughnut hole' county slivers and lacking full greenway trail construction.
side_a_arguments: Leave-behind county pockets complicate municipal service delivery and leave jagged jurisdictional boundaries.
Dedicating an easement without building the greenway segment misses an opportunity to connect active transportation links.
disagreements.side_b_position: Approve the consolidated annexation and rezoning for 30 missing-middle townhomes/duplexes.
side_b_arguments: The project provides needed missing-middle infill housing near major corridors alongside a $10,000 affordable housing fund contribution.
Planning Commission recommended approval 12-0 and the applicant worked within existing site constraints.
disagreements.resolution: Annexation and UEA passed 6-1 (Baker No); the companion zoning map change and consistency statement passed 7-0.

disagreements.meeting_title: Durham City Council Meeting May 19, 2025 (with closed captioning)
disagreements.issue: Peripheral Car-Centric Land Use Pattern and Advocacy Critique on Brier Creek Multifamily (Item 26)
disagreements.summary: Although Council ultimately approved the 408-unit Brier Creek Multifamily project 7-0, Council Members Baker and Freeman voiced sharp criticisms of peripheral car-centric growth and outside advocacy framing.
disagreements.side_a_position: Critique the broader land-use pattern of building dense apartments in car-dependent peripheral areas without transit and question outside YIMBY advocacy rhetoric.
side_a_arguments: Approving high-density housing on the Wake County border far from frequent transit entrenches automobile dependency (Baker).
Outside groups claiming to champion affordability often rubber-stamp market-rate development without building substantive partnerships with local affordable housing organizations (Freeman).
disagreements.side_b_position: Praise the developer's responsive proffers (5% at 80% AMI for 30 years, $50,000 housing fund, $16,500 DPS, native plantings) and support adding multifamily housing supply near jobs and retail.
side_b_arguments: The parcel sits inside existing city boundaries adjacent to existing Brier Creek commercial retail and employment corridors.
The applicant increased school and housing commitments directly in response to neighborhood and Planning Commission feedback.
disagreements.resolution: Despite policy reservations expressed during debate, all seven members voted Aye on the zoning map change, UEA, and consistency statement (7-0).

meetings.title: Durham City Council Work Session for May 8, 2025
meetings.executive_summary: At the May 8, 2025 work session with six members present and Mayor Pro Tempore Mark-Anthony Middleton previously excused, Council granted an excused absence for Council Member Javiera Caballero for May 22, accepted the City Manager's priority items, and voted 6-0 to hold a closed session on *Town of Chapel Hill v. City of Durham*. Council reviewed pulled consent items covering the FY 2026 Planning Work Program, Legal Aid DEAR contract, Hillandale Golf Course driving range expansion, the Cultural Roadmap timeline, and conveying surplus skate park equipment to The Scrap Exchange, and heard the Durham Racial Equity Commission's 2024 Annual Report highlighting wealth, traffic-stop, jury, and housing disparities. Council then discussed and placed Mayor Williams's resolution opposing NC House Bill 765 onto the May 19 General Business Agenda and settled the May 19 agenda 6-0 before entering closed session.

agenda_items.title: Roll Call, Excused Absence Request, Priority Items, and Closed Session Motion
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Mayor Leonardo Williams convened the session with six members present and Mark-Anthony Middleton previously excused. Council approved an excused absence for Javiera Caballero for May 22 (6-0), received the City Manager's priority items—Item 5 DREC Annual Report and Item 24 FY 2025-26 Budget presentation (6-0)—and approved holding a closed session at the end of the meeting regarding *Town of Chapel Hill v. City of Durham*, 85 CVS 3108 (6-0).

agenda_items.title: Citizen Matters
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Two speakers addressed Council during Citizen Matters: Robin raised concerns about OEWD delayed grant disbursements via MFA for small business/workforce services, and DeWarren Langley of the Charles Hamilton Houston Foundation discussed community initiatives.

agenda_items.title: Pulled Consent Items 3 and 4 (FY26 Planning Work Program & Legal Aid DEAR Contract)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Council Members Baker and Rist questioned planning staff on Item 3 (FY 2026 Planning Work Program) regarding UDO rewrite sequencing and staffing bandwidth, while Council Member Rist asked questions on Item 4 regarding the Legal Aid of North Carolina / Durham Expunction and Restoration (DEAR) contract.

agenda_items.title: Durham Racial Equity Commission (DREC) 2024 Annual Report
agenda_items.discussion_summary: DREC representatives Nisha Williams and Elena Snavely presented the commission's 2024 report examining disparities across criminal legal systems (traffic stops and jury inclusivity with Duke Sanford/Clerk of Court), housing, health, and wealth, recommending bold policies such as rent stabilization, guaranteed income expansion, and livable wages. Council members engaged in substantive discussion over local wealth data sources, Duke University contributions, bold policymaking without fear of state backlash, and whether future reports should include resident-facing recommendations alongside institutional reforms.

agenda_items.title: Pulled Consent Items 13, 15, and 18 (Hillandale Golf, Cultural Roadmap, Scrap Exchange Skate Park)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Council questioned staff on Item 13 (design-build renovation of Hillandale Golf Course's driving range and putting area benefiting youth programs like Swing Pals and First Tee), Item 15 (extending Phase 3 of the Cultural Roadmap into late fall 2025/spring 2026 after a four-year process), and Item 18 (donating surplus Wheels modular skate park ramps under N.C.G.S. 160A-280 to The Scrap Exchange for a free public skate park).

agenda_items.title: Resolution Opposing NC House Bill 765 and Settling May 19, 2025 Agenda
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Mayor Leonardo Williams introduced Item 27 opposing North Carolina House Bill 765 alongside bipartisan I-85 Corridor mayors and the NC League of Municipalities, with Council Members Freeman and Caballero strongly endorsing the defense of Section 160D local land-use powers. Council then settled the May 19 meeting agenda (Consent Items 1-23; GBA Items 24 & 27; GBA Public Hearings 25 & 26) by 6-0 voice vote and recessed into closed session at 3:00 PM.

votes.item_title: Excused Absence for Council Member Javiera Caballero for May 22, 2025 Work Session
votes.notes: Mark-Anthony Middleton was absent (previously excused on May 5).
votes.discussion_detail: Near the opening of the May 8 work session, Council Member Javiera Caballero requested an excused absence in advance for the upcoming May 22, 2025 work session. With Mayor Pro Tempore Middleton absent on a previously approved excuse, six council members were present. Following a motion and second, Council unanimously granted Caballero's excused absence by a 6-0 voice vote.

votes.item_title: Motion to Receive City Manager's Priority Items (Items 5 and 24)
votes.notes: Priority Items: Item 5 (DREC 2024 Annual Report) at May 8 work session; Item 24 (FY25-26 Proposed Budget & CIP) at May 19 Council meeting.
votes.discussion_detail: City Manager Bo Ferguson presented two priority items for Council's schedule: Item 5, the Durham Racial Equity Commission's 2024 Annual Report for immediate presentation at the work session, and Item 24, the FY 2025-26 Proposed Budget and FY 2026-31 CIP presentation scheduled for the May 19 regular meeting. No objections or modifications were raised by members. Council unanimously voted 6-0 by voice vote to receive the priority items.

votes.item_title: Motion to Hold Closed Session (Town of Chapel Hill v. City of Durham, 85 CVS 3108)
votes.notes: Pursuant to N.C.G.S. 143-318.11(a)(3) for attorney-client consultation; held at end of meeting at 3:00 PM.
votes.discussion_detail: City Attorney staff requested a closed session at the conclusion of the May 8 work session pursuant to N.C.G.S. 143-318.11(a)(3) to consult with the City Attorney and preserve attorney-client privilege regarding pending litigation in *Town of Chapel Hill v. City of Durham*, Wake/Orange/Durham Superior Court file 85 CVS 3108. Council voted unanimously 6-0 by voice vote to authorize the closed session. After completing the public agenda, Mayor Williams confirmed the earlier vote and moved members into the Council conference room at 3:00 PM, adjourning afterward.

disagreements.meeting_title: Durham City Council Work Session for May 8, 2025
disagreements.issue: Scope of Durham Racial Equity Commission Recommendations: Institutional Change vs. Individual Action & Backlash Risk
disagreements.summary: Following DREC's 2024 Annual Report, Council members differed in emphasis between pushing bold structural policies regardless of state backlash, investigating Duke's tax/resource equity, and adding individual resident-level action steps.
disagreements.side_a_position: Focus squarely on bold institutional, wealth-disparity, rent-stabilization, and livable-wage reforms rather than legislating out of fear of state pushback or shifting responsibility onto individuals.
side_a_arguments: Racial equity work is fundamentally systemic because residents do not control government purse strings or macroeconomic structures.

Durham should lead boldly on policies like rent stabilization, wealth data tracking, and equitable contributions from major institutions like Duke rather than self-censoring over potential state backlash.
disagreements.side_b_position: Include parallel recommendations for individual residents alongside institutional reforms so residents also see steps to position themselves to access opportunities.
side_b_arguments: While government bears primary responsibility, having a complete picture requires empowering individuals with actionable steps to connect to programs and services.
disagreements.resolution: DREC presenters agreed to consider resident-facing guidance while reiterating that DREC's core charge is evaluating government institutions and policies.

meetings.title: Durham Joint City County Planning Committee (JCCPC) May 7, 2025
meetings.presiding_chair: Chair Jacobs (BOCC); Vice Chair Nate Baker
meetings.executive_summary: At the May 7, 2025 Joint City-County Planning Committee (JCCPC) meeting—chaired by County Commissioner Jacobs with Council Member Nate Baker serving as Vice Chair and Mayor Leonardo Williams attending as alternate for excused members Javiera Caballero and Mark-Anthony Middleton—the committee unanimously approved excused absences and the April 2 minutes. Staff presented the newly approved Vision Zero Action Plan and how it will integrate into the Unified Development Ordinance (UDO) rewrite, highlighting that 10% of Durham streets account for 74% of fatal and serious-injury crashes and disproportionate harm to Black residents. Members debated roadway design versus driver education, speed of quick-build safety installations, and density bonuses versus universal upzoning, heard a Module 2 UDO engagement update, and deferred the Historic Preservation Commission Interlocal Agreement back to staff for June.

agenda_items.title: Call to Order, Roll Call, Excused Absences, and Approval of April 2, 2025 Minutes
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chair Jacobs called the meeting to order at 9:35 AM with Vice Chair Nate Baker, alternate Mayor Leonardo Williams, and County/Planning members present; Javiera Caballero and Mark-Anthony Middleton were absent. The committee unanimously approved excused absences for Caballero and Middleton and approved the April 2, 2025 minutes.
agenda_items.vote_summary: Excused absences approved unanimously; Minutes approved unanimously

agenda_items.title: Vision Zero Action Plan and UDO Rewrite Integration
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Vision Zero Coordinator Lauren Grove and Principal Planner Robin Schultze presented crash statistics showing ~22 traffic deaths per year in Durham, with 10% of roadways (130 miles) accounting for 74% of deaths and serious injuries and Black residents comprising 49% of fatalities and 53% of serious injuries. They outlined proposed UDO rewrite tools including right-of-way street cross-section realignment, multimodal traffic impact analyses, context-sensitive block lengths, drive-through/curb-cut restrictions, and corridor safety density bonuses. Committee members debated driver behavior versus built-environment solutions, slow quick-build delivery, intersection demographics, and universal upzoning vs. density bonuses.

agenda_items.title: UDO Rewrite Module 2 Community Engagement Update
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Planning staff Lisa Miller summarized Module 2 engagement launching May 12 through early June 2025, featuring virtual webinars, in-person sessions at WG Pearson Center and Braggtown Community Center, four monthly library office-hour drop-ins, and updated district/place-type mapping. Members praised the accessible explainer materials and office hours.

agenda_items.title: Historic Preservation Commission Interlocal Agreement Referral
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Staff planner Carla Rosenberg reported that staff requested referring the Historic Preservation Commission Interlocal Agreement back to staff for further legal and administrative refinement before returning tentatively on June 4. Chair Jacobs and members asked that final drafts be posted 10 days ahead of the next meeting before adjourning.
agenda_items.vote_summary: Referred back to staff / No formal vote

votes.notes: Joint City-County committee; City Council members Nate Baker (Vice Chair) and Leonardo Williams (alternate) voted Aye alongside County Commissioners Jacobs, Lee, and Valentine and Planning Commissioner Cameron. Caballero and Middleton absent/excused.
votes.discussion_detail: During roll call at the start of the May 7 JCCPC meeting, Mayor Leonardo Williams—attending as the City Council alternate—requested excused absences for absent Council Members Javiera Caballero and Mayor Pro Tempore Mark-Anthony Middleton. Following a motion and second from committee members, Chair Jacobs called for a voice vote. All present City, County, and Planning members voted Aye, and the excused absences were unanimously approved.

votes.item_title: Approval of April 2, 2025 JCCPC Meeting Minutes
votes.notes: Joint City-County committee; Baker and Williams represent City Council members voting Aye alongside County and Planning members.
votes.discussion_detail: Chair Jacobs asked whether any members had revisions or corrections to the draft minutes of the April 2, 2025 JCCPC meeting. Hearing none, Vice Chair Nate Baker moved to approve the minutes as presented, and Mayor Leonardo Williams seconded the motion. The committee approved the minutes unanimously by voice vote.

disagreements.meeting_title: Durham Joint City County Planning Committee (JCCPC) May 7, 2025
disagreements.issue: Vision Zero Implementation: Driver Behavior Education vs. Street Design, Quick-Build Delays, and Density Bonuses
disagreements.summary: JCCPC members differed on whether driver education or physical street engineering should carry priority in Vision Zero, while Vice Chair Baker and Mayor Williams challenged staff on right-of-way splits, density bonuses, and quick-build execution speed.
disagreements.side_a_position: Question emphasizing driver behavior/education vs. built environment, or challenge density bonuses and right-of-way allocations that prioritize cars over multimodal street space.
side_a_arguments: Commissioner Lee asked why driver education sits higher on the safe-systems pyramid when reckless driving causes crashes.

Nate Baker argued against relying on density bonuses for basic pedestrian safety instead of universal upzoning and urged dedicating at least 50% of right-of-way space to multimodal/pedestrian infrastructure rather than mostly cars.
disagreements.side_b_position: Focus on systemic street engineering, rapid quick-build interventions in Black-majority high-injury corridors, and practical incremental UDO incentives.
side_b_arguments: Lauren Grove explained public-health evidence shows changing roadway geometry and speeds protects everyone regardless of human error.

Leonardo Williams pressed staff for the top 10 dangerous intersections by neighborhood demographics and demanded accelerating physical quick-build barriers rather than waiting years for full rebuilds.
disagreements.resolution: Informational workshop item; staff committed to sharing top-10 intersection racial/demographic data and incorporating committee feedback into UDO Module 2/3 drafts and Multimodal TIA budget requests.

meetings.title: Durham City Council May 5, 2025 (full meeting with closed captioning)
meetings.executive_summary: With all seven council members present, Council issued proclamations for Huntington's Disease Awareness Month and National Drinking Water Week, granted Mayor Pro Tempore Mark-Anthony Middleton an excused absence for the May 8 work session (7-0), and adopted the Consent Agenda 7-0. Council unanimously approved the 95-unit Strauss Drive Townhouses rezoning (7-0) before spending nearly three hours on Item 15, the 86.41-acre Howard Property consolidated annexation and rezoning on Wake Forest Highway (NC 98) proposing up to 499 residential units and 12,000 square feet of commercial space. Following extensive opposition from Preserve Rural Durham, environmental advocates, and neighbors—offset by the Howard, Jones, and Height landowner families and five last-minute applicant proffers—Council narrowly approved the annexation and rezoning 4-3 (Baker, Cook, and Freeman dissenting) before passing the statutory consistency statement 7-0.

agenda_items.title: Roll Call, Proclamations, Excused Absence, and Announcements
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Mayor Leonardo Williams opened the meeting with all seven council members present, presenting proclamations for Huntington's Disease Awareness Month (Council Member Cook) and National Drinking Water Week (Mayor Pro Tempore Middleton). Council approved Middleton's excused absence for the May 8 work session (7-0), and Mayor Williams previewed an upcoming resolution opposing NC House Bill 765.

agenda_items.title: Priority Items and Consent Agenda Adoption
agenda_items.discussion_summary: City Manager Bo Ferguson reported added information for Consent Items 6 (DPR Comprehensive Park System Plan), 9 (Pavement Management Contract ST-335C), and 13 (Proposed Water and Sewer Rates) requested on April 24. Mayor Williams swapped the hearing order of Items 16 and 15 on GBA and read the Consent Agenda (Items 1-13), which Council adopted unanimously 7-0.

agenda_items.title: Zoning Map Change – Strauss Drive Townhouses (1801-1850 Strauss Drive)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Planner Andy Lester and applicant attorney Marie Farmer (Parker Poe for Profit Dixon Partners) presented a 13.49-acre rezoning from CC and RS-20 to RS-M(D) and CC(D) to permit up to 95 townhouse, detached, or multiplex units near South Miami Boulevard transit and retail. Commitments included 5% of units at 80% AMI for 30 years, 70% maximum impervious surface, 25% tree coverage, 100% native plantings, and a DPS contribution; Planning Commission recommended approval 8-0, and Council approved 7-0.

agenda_items.title: Consolidated Annexation – Howard Property (Z2300011 / BDG2300007, Wake Forest Hwy / NC 98)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Planning staff and Dan Jewell (Thomas & Hutton for Highway 98 East Durham LLC) presented a 10-parcel, 86.41-acre annexation and rezoning from RR and RS-20 to PDR 5.783 inside the Urban Growth Boundary for up to 499 units and 12,000 square feet of commercial space. Roughly 15 opponents including Preserve Rural Durham and Neuse Riverkeeper Samantha Krop warned of Lick Creek/Falls Lake sediment pollution, natural heritage fragmentation, NC 98 congestion, EMS strain, and inaccurate stream disclosures in the staff report, while landowners Larry Howard, Kelly Jones, and Robert Height Jr. testified for property rights and community investment. After the applicant added five commitments—including raising affordable housing to 6% and capping impervious cover at 50%—Council approved annexation and rezoning 4-3 and the consistency statement 7-0.

votes.item_title: Excused Absence for Mayor Pro Tempore Mark-Anthony Middleton (May 8, 2025 Work Session)
votes.notes: Excused absence granted in advance for May 8 work session.
votes.discussion_detail: Before moving into routine business, Mayor Williams noted that Mayor Pro Tempore Mark-Anthony Middleton needed to request an excused absence in advance for the upcoming Thursday, May 8 work session due to a scheduling conflict. No members objected to granting the advance excuse. Following a motion and second, the Council voted electronically and approved the excused absence unanimously 7-0.

votes.item_title: Item 16: UDO Zoning Map Change (CC & RS-20 to RS-M(D) and CC(D)) – Strauss Drive Townhouses
votes.notes: 13.49 acres (1801-1850 Strauss Dr); up to 95 units; 5% at 80% AMI 30 years; 70% max impervious; 25% tree coverage; 100% native plantings.
votes.discussion_detail: Planner Andy Lester and applicant attorney Marie Farmer presented the Strauss Drive Townhouses rezoning, converting vacant commercial-center parcels near South Miami Boulevard into RS-M(D) and CC(D) to permit up to 95 attached or multifamily units. Proffers included 5% of units affordable at 80% AMI for 30 years, 70% maximum impervious coverage, 25% tree coverage preservation, 100% native plantings, and a DPS contribution, with Planning Commission backing approval 8-0. With no public opposition, Council approved the rezoning unanimously 7-0.

votes.item_title: Item 16: Consistency Statement (N.C.G.S. 160D-605) – Strauss Drive Townhouses
votes.notes: Consistent with Transit Opportunity Area place type.
votes.discussion_detail: Following approval of the Strauss Drive Townhouses zoning map ordinance, Council considered the statutory consistency statement required by N.C.G.S. Section 160D-605. Planning staff confirmed the requested zoning aligned with the site's Transit Opportunity Area place type designation on the Comprehensive Plan map. Council approved the consistency statement unanimously 7-0.

votes.item_title: Item 15: Annexation Ordinance and Utility Extension Agreement – Howard Property
votes.notes: 10 parcels / 86.41 acres on NC 98 / Wake Forest Hwy (Highway 98 East Durham LLC).
votes.discussion_detail: After nearly three hours of testimony from roughly 15 opponents warning of Lick Creek/Falls Lake sedimentation, wildlife corridor fragmentation, NC 98 traffic, EMS delays, and an initial staff-report error stating no streams were on site—countered by landowners Larry Howard, Kelly Jones, and Robert Height Jr.—applicant Dan Jewell added five commitments including raising affordable units from 5% to 6% and capping impervious cover at 50%. Council Members Baker, Cook, and Freeman opposed annexation citing environmental vulnerability, greenfield infrastructure strain, and transparency flaws. Mayor Williams, Mayor Pro Tempore Middleton, Caballero, and Rist supported annexation citing Urban Growth Boundary alignment, housing need, and landowner rights, passing the ordinance 4-3.

votes.item_title: Item 15: UDO Zoning Map Change Ordinance (RR & RS-20 County to PDR 5.783 City) – Howard Property
votes.notes: Includes Falls/Jordan District B Watershed Overlay; DeDreana Freeman's button failed to register and her Nay vote was verbally confirmed for the record at 03:53:25.
votes.discussion_detail: Following the 4-3 annexation vote, Council voted on the companion UDO Zoning Map Change converting the 86.41-acre Howard Property from RR and RS-20 County to PDR 5.783 City with Falls/Jordan District B Watershed Overlay for up to 499 units and 12,000 square feet of commercial space. Council Member Freeman's voting console briefly failed to register electronically, so Mayor Williams and the Clerk verbally confirmed her Nay vote for the official record. The rezoning passed on the same 4-3 split, with Williams, Middleton, Caballero, and Rist voting Aye and Baker, Cook, and Freeman voting Nay.

votes.item_title: Item 15: Consistency Statement (N.C.G.S. 160D-605) – Howard Property
votes.notes: Unanimous statutory consistency finding despite 4-3 vote on project approval; adjourned at 10:54 PM.
votes.discussion_detail: To close the Howard Property item, Council voted on the statutory consistency statement required under N.C.G.S. Section 160D-605 confirming the zoning change's consistency with Durham's Comprehensive Plan. Although three members opposed the annexation and rezoning on environmental and infrastructure grounds, all seven members voted in favor of the procedural consistency finding. The motion passed unanimously 7-0 and Mayor Williams adjourned the meeting at 10:54 PM.

disagreements.meeting_title: Durham City Council May 5, 2025 (full meeting with closed captioning)
disagreements.issue: Howard Property Consolidated Annexation and Rezoning (Item 15): Greenfield Watershed Impact vs. Urban Growth Boundary Housing Supply
disagreements.summary: A 4-3 split divided Council over annexing and rezoning 86.41 acres along NC 98 in the Lick Creek/Falls Lake watershed for up to 499 residential units and 12,000 sq ft of commercial space.
disagreements.side_a_position: Approve the consolidated annexation and PDR 5.783 rezoning with five added applicant proffers.
side_a_arguments: The site sits inside the Urban Growth Boundary designated for Suburban Neighborhood/Community Commercial development in the newly adopted Comprehensive Plan.
The applicant added substantial concessions at the hearing: 6% affordable housing (up from 5%), 50% impervious cap, 25-year stormwater controls, native plantings, and playgrounds.
Supporting the project respects the property rights of the long-time Howard, Jones, and Height landowner families and expands housing near jobs.
disagreements.side_b_position: Deny the annexation and rezoning due to environmental degradation in the Lick Creek/Falls Lake watershed, traffic/EMS constraints, and staff-report inaccuracies.
side_b_arguments: The site lies in a fragile Lick Creek natural heritage corridor draining toward Falls Lake, and staff's packet initially misstated that no streams existed on site.
NC 98 faces severe traffic congestion and rural 911/EMS response strain that 499 more units will worsen without adequate transit.
Major design changes and stream/environmental disclosures were introduced too late for thorough public transparency.
disagreements.resolution: Annexation/UEA and zoning map change both passed 4-3; consistency statement passed 7-0.

meetings.title: Durham City Council Work Session April 24, 2025
meetings.executive_summary: With Mayor Leonardo Williams absent on excused city travel, Mayor Pro Tempore Mark-Anthony Middleton presided over the April 24 work session with six council members present. Council heard citizen complaints regarding climate disaster preparedness, Vision Zero safety after fatal crashes on Roxboro Street, and commercial trucks parking on Dakota Street near Shepard Middle School, and examined pulled consent items on the 2025 Comprehensive Park System Plan (including Elmira Park tennis court deterioration), pavement management accountability, and VMware licensing. Department of Water Management Director Don Greeley presented an 8.5% average FY 2025-26 water and sewer rate increase driven by rising construction costs and the near-$1 billion Jordan Lake treatment project, followed by a Parks and Recreation presentation on the Durham Central Park Concept Plan before Council settled the May 5 meeting agenda 6-0.

agenda_items.title: Opening, Roll Call, Announcements, and Agenda Reading
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Mayor Pro Tempore Mark-Anthony Middleton convened the work session at 1:00 PM with six members present (Mayor Williams absent/excused for city business) and Deputy City Manager Bertha Wimbush and Deputy City Attorney present. Council Member Rist announced Triangle West TPO's adoption of a regional safety action plan and 2055 MTP projections (90% job growth, 48% population growth) as well as Downtown Durham Inc.'s Blueprint 2035 launch; priority items and board nominations were read, and Consent Items 6, 9, and 11 were pulled.

agenda_items.title: Citizen Matters
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Residents addressed Council regarding PAC 1 and PAC 5 climate-change disaster preparedness training (Aisha Abdul-Ali and James Chavis requesting city response to a disaster preparedness proclamation), Vision Zero roadway engineering urgency after a crosswalk near-miss and three fatalities on Roxboro Street (Chris Perilstein), and commercial 18-wheeler/box-truck parking and speeding on Dakota Street adjacent to Shepard Middle School (Jacqueline Wagstaff).

agenda_items.title: Pulled Consent Items 6, 9, and 11 (Park Plan / Elmira Courts, Pavement Management, VMware Licenses)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Five speakers including RAC member Dale McKielle and tennis players Chris Foster, Melvin Talbert, Katarina Raher, and Mike Gallagher spoke on Item 6 urging half-penny parks funding and proper subsurface drainage for cracked Elmira Park tennis courts. On Item 9 (ST-335C Pavement Management Services), speaker Dale McKielle questioned bike-lane buffer striping errors on MLK Parkway and peeling pavement preservation surfaces; Public Works' Tasha Johnson attributed peeling to subsurface conditions and noted contractor recourse. On Item 11 (CDW/VMware data center licensing), Technology Solutions' Dwayne Kendall explained the five-year refresh cycle ahead of cloud migration.

agenda_items.title: Proposed FY 2025-26 Water and Sewer Rates Presentation
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Water Management Director Don Greeley proposed an overall 8.5% water/sewer rate increase (+$2.41/month for a typical Tier 1 customer) and projected 11.25% future annual increases driven by 80% construction inflation and a ~$2 billion five-year capital program—nearly half for the generational Jordan Lake intake, treatment plant, and 17-mile pipeline. Greeley also noted Sanford's merger with Pittsboro/Chatham County affects Jordan Lake governance cost recovery, while CFO Tim Flora noted the Water Hardship Fund holds a ~$400,000 cumulative balance with demand easing below $100,000 year-to-date. Council asked about governance agreements, tier usage breakdowns, federal/state grant advocacy, PFAS/1,4-dioxane readiness, and bill calculators.

agenda_items.title: Proposed Durham Central Park Concept Plan Presentation
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Parks and Recreation staff presented a three-phase concept plan for Durham Central Park envisioning upgraded gardens, Canopy Plaza, Sister Cities Grove, an interactive water feature, great lawn upgrades, and permanently converting Foster Street into a pedestrian Festival Street with food-truck electrical hookups. Council members praised the plan's vision, urged retaining the skate park without displacing youth, discussed affordable housing on adjacent city-owned parcels (former Substation 5), suggested wayfinding signage and unhoused shower/locker facilities, and inquired about phasing costs and downtown loop connections.

agenda_items.title: Settling the May 5, 2025 City Council Meeting Agenda
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Deputy City Manager Bertha Wimbush proposed placing Items 1 through 13 on Consent and Items 15 (Howard Property) and 16 (Strauss Drive Townhouses) as GBA public hearings for the May 5 meeting. Council unanimously approved settling the agenda 6-0 and adjourned at 3:18 PM.

meetings.title: Durham City Council April 21, 2025 with closed captioning
meetings.executive_summary: With all seven members present, the Durham City Council issued four ceremonial proclamations, added Priority Item 24 (a DEQ recycling grant ordinance) to the consent agenda, and adopted the consent agenda 7-0 before approving two pulled consent items—the water/sewer connection code amendment and Corporate F.A.C.T.S. Consolidated Plan contract—also 7-0. Council unanimously approved substantial CDBG and HOPWA Consolidated Plan amendments (7-0) and four major land-use items including the staff-initiated Page/Miami Design District (five votes at 7-0), a private UDO text amendment allowing tree-coverage adjustments via statutory development agreements (7-0), the 100% affordable 160-unit Page Corners apartment project (7-0), and 1202 Ellis Road (7-0). On Item 18 (Romero Residence), Council debated whether to extend water/sewer to non-contiguous lots without annexation, ultimately approving the annexation/UEA 7-0 and passing the zoning map change 6-1 with Council Member Chelsea Cook voting No.

agenda_items.title: Roll Call, Proclamations, Announcements, and Priority Item 24
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Mayor Leonardo Williams called the meeting to order with all seven members present and presented proclamations for Tuberous Sclerosis Complex Day, the Community Partner Development Course graduation, Fair Housing Month, and National Community Development Week. Council unanimously added Priority Item 24 (DEQ Community Waste Reduction and Recycling Grant Project Ordinance) to the consent agenda (7-0).

agenda_items.title: Consent Agenda and Pulled Items 5 & 6
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Council adopted the consent agenda (Items 1-4, 7-18, 24) 7-0 on a motion by Chelsea Cook seconded by Mark-Anthony Middleton. Council then debated pulled Item 5 (water/sewer connection code amendment, speakers Katie Ross and Tina Motley-Pearson) and pulled Item 6 (Corporate F.A.C.T.S. Consolidated Plan consulting contract, speaker Alejandro Ruiz urging deeper community language/stakeholder engagement), approving both items unanimously 7-0.

agenda_items.title: Substantial Amendments to FY 2020-2025 Consolidated Plan & Annual Action Plans (CDBG/HOPWA)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Community Development staff presented substantial amendments reallocating CDBG and HOPWA funds, with public speakers (Tiffany Swope, Carolyn Hinton, Crystal Graves, and Dr. Haley Cunningham) highlighting homelessness, supportive services, and HIV/AIDS housing needs. Council approved the amendments unanimously 7-0.

agenda_items.title: Consolidated Annexation – Romero Residence (213 Scheer Avenue)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Staff presented a 0.64-acre non-contiguous satellite annexation and utility extension request for a single-family home at 213 Scheer Avenue owned by Jorge Jacobo Romero and Guadalupe Lopez Juarez. Council Members Cook and Baker argued utility connections should not require annexing isolated county lots, while Middleton, Caballero, and Freeman emphasized state legislative restrictions preventing future annexation if skipped; Council approved annexation/UEA 7-0, zoning 6-1 (Cook No), and consistency 7-0.

agenda_items.title: Consolidated Item – Page/Miami Design District (TC2400002 & Z2400018)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Senior Planner Kayla Seibel presented a 25.41-acre city-initiated rezoning and UDO text amendment establishing the Page/Miami Design District in southeast Durham near RTP, requested earlier by JCCPC. Council unanimously approved all five required actions (text amendment, text consistency, zoning map change, map consistency, and Comprehensive Plan place-type resolution) 7-0.

agenda_items.title: UDO Text Amendment – Tree Coverage Adjustments via Statutory Development Agreements (TC2400003)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Planning staff Robin Schultze and attorney Patrick Byker (for Lincoln Avenue Communities) presented a privately initiated text amendment allowing Statutory Development Agreements to modify UDO Section 8.3 tree coverage/protection standards in exchange for binding public benefits such as 100% affordable housing. Council approved the ordinance and consistency statement 7-0.

agenda_items.title: Consolidated Annexation – Page Corners (4004 & 4110 Page Road, Z2400027)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Council considered the 7.602-acre Page Corners consolidated annexation, PDR 22.456 rezoning, and companion Statutory Development Agreement for 160 multifamily apartments restricted 100% affordable at or below 60% AMI for 30 years. Using the newly enabled SDA authority under Item 20, the project reduced open space (20% to 15%) and tree coverage (20% to 7%) while upgrading fencing to 6 feet; Council approved all three votes 7-0.

agenda_items.title: Zoning Map Change – 1202 Ellis Road
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Dan Jewell presented a 1.24-acre rezoning from RR to RS-M(D) for up to 20 single-family or duplex units at 1202 Ellis Road, adding a binding commitment at the hearing that at least 50% of units be attached or duplex dwellings. Council approved the rezoning and consistency statement 7-0 before adjourning at 10:43 PM.

votes.item_title: Item 5: City Code Amendment for Water and Sewer Connections
votes.notes: Pulled by public speakers Katie Ross and Tina Motley-Pearson.
votes.discussion_detail: Item 5, an ordinance amending City Code provisions governing water and sewer connections, was pulled from consent by public speakers Katie Ross and Tina Motley-Pearson, who raised questions regarding rural connection policy, affordability, and annexation ties. Water Management and planning staff clarified the scope of the technical code update for Council and residents. Following public comment, Mayor Pro Tempore Middleton moved approval, Council Member Rist seconded, and the amendment passed unanimously 7-0.

votes.item_title: Item 6: Contract with Corporate F.A.C.T.S., Inc. for 2025-2029 Consolidated Plan
votes.notes: Pulled by public speaker Alejandro Ruiz.
votes.discussion_detail: Item 6 authorized a consulting contract with Corporate F.A.C.T.S., Inc. to prepare the city's 2025-2029 HUD Consolidated Plan and was pulled for comment by speaker Alejandro Ruiz, who urged broader community engagement, multilingual outreach, and accountability for resident input. Council members and Community Development staff noted the importance of broad stakeholder participation as the five-year federal housing and community development plan is drafted. On a motion and second, Council approved the contract unanimously 7-0.

votes.item_title: Item 23: Substantial Amendments to FY 2020-2025 Consolidated Plan and Annual Action Plans (CDBG & HOPWA)
votes.notes: Public hearing held with testimony from Tiffany Swope, Carolyn Hinton, Crystal Graves, and Dr. Haley Cunningham.
votes.discussion_detail: Community Development staff presented substantial federal grant amendments reprogramming Community Development Block Grant (CDBG) and Housing Opportunities for Persons With AIDS (HOPWA) funds within the FY 2020-2025 Consolidated Plan and Annual Action Plans. Four public speakers—Tiffany Swope, Carolyn Hinton, Crystal Graves, and Dr. Haley Cunningham—addressed urgent community housing stability, medical/supportive care, and HIV/AIDS housing needs during the public hearing. Following the hearing and brief council remarks, Council unanimously approved the substantial amendments 7-0.

votes.item_title: Item 18: Annexation Ordinance and Utility Extension Agreement – Romero Residence (213 Scheer Ave)
votes.notes: 0.64 acres non-contiguous lot; UEA with Jorge Jacobo Romero and Guadalupe Lopez Juarez.
votes.discussion_detail: Council held a public hearing on the 0.64-acre non-contiguous consolidated annexation and Utility Extension Agreement for the single-family Romero Residence at 213 Scheer Avenue, presented with representative Joshua Jacobo. Council Members Cook and Baker questioned extending water/sewer service via UEA without annexing an isolated satellite parcel, whereas Middleton, Caballero, and Freeman argued state legislative restrictions could prevent Durham from ever annexing the property later if skipped. Ultimately, all seven members voted Aye on the annexation and utility extension agreement, passing it 7-0.

votes.item_title: Item 18: UDO Zoning Map Change (RS-20 County to RS-20 City) – Romero Residence
votes.notes: Includes Falls/Jordan District B Watershed Overlay conversion from County to City jurisdiction; Chelsea Cook voted No.
votes.discussion_detail: Immediately following the unanimous annexation/UEA vote for 213 Scheer Avenue, Council voted on the companion UDO Zoning Map Change transferring the parcel from RS-20 Falls/Jordan District B Watershed Overlay County jurisdiction to RS-20 City jurisdiction. Council Member Chelsea Cook voted No, maintaining her objection to non-contiguous satellite zoning/annexation mechanics even though the underlying single-family residential district remained unchanged. Six members voted Aye and the zoning ordinance passed 6-1.

votes.item_title: Item 18: Consistency Statement (N.C.G.S. 160D-605) – Romero Residence
votes.notes: Statutory consistency finding under N.C.G.S. 160D-605.
votes.discussion_detail: To complete the Romero Residence consolidated annexation case, Council voted on the statutory consistency statement under N.C.G.S. Section 160D-605 affirming alignment with Durham's Comprehensive Plan. Having expressed her policy concern on the zoning vote, Council Member Cook joined the rest of Council on the statutory finding. The consistency statement passed unanimously 7-0.

votes.item_title: Item 19: UDO Text Amendment (TC2400002, Articles 11 & 16) – Page/Miami Design District
votes.notes: Staff-initiated design district regulations requested by JCCPC ahead of UDO rewrite.
votes.discussion_detail: Senior Planner Kayla Seibel presented Item 19, a city-initiated consolidated package requested by the Joint City-County Planning Committee to establish the 25.41-acre Page/Miami Design District southeast of RTP between NC 54, Davis Drive, Hopson Road, Page Road, and South Miami Boulevard. Staff reviewed design standards and form-based regulations created in Articles 11 and 16 to encourage walkable mixed-use development ahead of the broader UDO rewrite. Council voted unanimously 7-0 to adopt the UDO text amendment ordinance.

votes.item_title: Item 19: Consistency Statement (N.C.G.S. 160D-605) for TC2400002 – Page/Miami Design District
votes.notes: Statutory consistency finding for UDO text amendment TC2400002.
votes.discussion_detail: Following approval of the Page/Miami Design District UDO text amendment (TC2400002), Council considered the accompanying statutory consistency statement under N.C.G.S. 160D-605. Planning staff confirmed the text amendment advances Comprehensive Plan objectives for mixed-use transit-oriented employment hubs. On a motion and second, the consistency statement passed unanimously 7-0.

votes.item_title: Item 19: UDO Zoning Map Change (Z2400018) – Page/Miami Design District
votes.notes: City-initiated rezoning applying Page/Miami Design District across 25.41 acres.
votes.discussion_detail: Council next acted on Z2400018, the city-initiated zoning map change applying the newly created Page/Miami Design District zoning across the 25.41-acre corridor near RTP. Members commended planning staff for executing the proactive JCCPC-requested area rezoning ahead of the UDO overhaul. The zoning map ordinance passed unanimously 7-0.

votes.item_title: Item 19: Consistency Statement (N.C.G.S. 160D-605) for Z2400018 – Page/Miami Design District
votes.notes: Statutory consistency finding for Z2400018.
votes.discussion_detail: To accompany zoning map change Z2400018 for the Page/Miami Design District, Council considered the formal consistency statement under N.C.G.S. Section 160D-605. No further questions or objections were raised following the presentation and prior votes. Council unanimously adopted the consistency statement 7-0.

votes.item_title: Item 19: Comprehensive Plan Place Type Amendment Resolution – Page/Miami Design District
votes.notes: Updates Comprehensive Plan Place Type map to align with Design District.
votes.discussion_detail: As the fifth and final action on the consolidated Page/Miami Design District item, Council voted on the resolution amending the Comprehensive Plan Place Type map to align the 25.41-acre area with the new design district designation. Staff confirmed all notices and public hearing requirements had been fulfilled. Council unanimously approved the resolution 7-0.

votes.item_title: Item 20: UDO Text Amendment Ordinance (TC2400003, Tree Coverage via Statutory Development Agreements)
votes.notes: Privately initiated text amendment (Lincoln Avenue Communities / Patrick Byker) amending Article 3 to allow Statutory Development Agreements to adjust Sec. 8.3 tree coverage/protection.
votes.discussion_detail: Planning staff Robin Schultze and applicant attorney Patrick Byker (representing Lincoln Avenue Communities) presented TC2400003, a privately initiated UDO Article 3 text amendment permitting Statutory Development Agreements (SDAs) to alter Section 8.3 tree coverage and protection standards when tied to high-priority public benefits such as 100% affordable housing. Council members questioned potential precedent beyond affordable housing and noted SDAs require explicit Council approval, preserving legislative control over each case. Satisfied with that safeguard, Council passed the text amendment unanimously 7-0.

votes.item_title: Item 20: Consistency Statement (N.C.G.S. 160D-605) – TC2400003
votes.notes: Statutory consistency finding for UDO text amendment TC2400003.
votes.discussion_detail: Following passage of UDO text amendment TC2400003 enabling Statutory Development Agreement flexibility on tree coverage, Council voted on the companion N.C.G.S. Section 160D-605 consistency statement. Staff confirmed consistency with Comprehensive Plan housing and procedural goals. Council adopted the consistency statement unanimously 7-0.

votes.item_title: Item 21: Annexation Ordinance – Page Corners (4004 & 4110 Page Road)
votes.notes: 7.602 acres for 160-unit 100% affordable multifamily community (<=60% AMI for 30 years).
votes.discussion_detail: Council heard Item 21, the 7.602-acre Page Corners consolidated annexation and affordable housing proposal at 4004 and 4110 Page Road developed by Page Road Apartments, LP (Lincoln Avenue Communities). The development delivers 160 multifamily units 100% income-restricted at or below 60% AMI for 30 years. Welcoming the dedicated affordable housing supply, Council unanimously approved the annexation ordinance 7-0.

votes.item_title: Item 21: UDO Zoning Map Change (PDR 22.456), Statutory Development Agreement, and UEA – Page Corners
votes.notes: Z2400027; SDA reduces open space 20%->15% and tree coverage 20%->7%, changes fence 4ft->6ft, and waives Frontier buffer in exchange for 100% affordability at <=60% AMI for 30 years.
votes.discussion_detail: Council next voted on the combined motion adopting the Z2400027 rezoning to PDR 22.456, the Statutory Development Agreement enabled by Item 20, and the Utility Extension Agreement with Page Road Apartments, LP. Under the SDA, the site reduces required open space from 20% to 15% and tree coverage from 20% to 7%, increases privacy fencing from four to six feet, and waives a perimeter buffer along Frontier in exchange for binding 30-year 100% affordability at or below 60% AMI. Council members praised the creative trade-off securing 160 deeply affordable homes and approved the motion unanimously 7-0.

votes.item_title: Item 21: Consistency Statement (N.C.G.S. 160D-605) – Page Corners
votes.notes: Statutory consistency finding for Z2400027.
votes.discussion_detail: To finalize the Page Corners affordable housing approval, Council considered the statutory consistency statement under N.C.G.S. Section 160D-605 confirming the PDR 22.456 zoning and Statutory Development Agreement align with the Comprehensive Plan. No additional debate occurred. Council adopted the consistency statement unanimously 7-0.

votes.item_title: Item 22: UDO Zoning Map Change (RR to RS-M(D)) – 1202 Ellis Road
votes.notes: 1.24 acres; up to 20 single-family/duplex units.
votes.discussion_detail: Applicant representative Dan Jewell presented Item 22, rezoning 1.24 acres at 1202 Ellis Road from Rural Residential (RR) to Residential Suburban Multifamily with Development Plan (RS-M(D)) to allow up to 20 residential units. During council questioning regarding housing mix and missing-middle form, the applicant proffered an added text commitment guaranteeing at least 50% of units would be attached or duplex dwellings. Council welcomed the binding housing-type commitment and approved the zoning ordinance unanimously 7-0.

votes.item_title: Item 22: Consistency Statement (N.C.G.S. 160D-605) – 1202 Ellis Road
votes.notes: Statutory consistency finding under N.C.G.S. 160D-605; meeting adjourned at 10:43 PM.
votes.discussion_detail: To close out the 1202 Ellis Road rezoning and the April 21 docket, Council voted on the statutory consistency statement under N.C.G.S. Section 160D-605. Planning staff confirmed consistency with Durham's Comprehensive Plan Place Type map and middle-housing policies. The consistency statement passed unanimously 7-0, and Mayor Williams adjourned the meeting at 10:43 PM.

disagreements.meeting_title: Durham City Council April 21, 2025 with closed captioning
disagreements.issue: Annexing vs. Extending Utilities Without Annexation for Non-Contiguous Single-Family Lot (Item 18: Romero Residence)
disagreements.summary: Council debated whether non-contiguous properties seeking city water and sewer connections should be annexed into city limits or served solely through Utility Extension Agreements, leading to a 6-1 vote on the zoning conversion.
disagreements.side_a_position: Question annexing isolated non-contiguous parcels and prefer extending utilities via UEA without mandatory municipal boundary expansion (Cook voted No on City zoning conversion).
side_a_arguments: Creating non-contiguous satellite pockets complicates municipal boundaries and service delivery.
Extending utility service to an existing single-family home via UEA can achieve public health and utility goals without satellite annexation.
disagreements.side_b_position: Proceed with consolidated annexation alongside the UEA because North Carolina state law restricts future involuntary annexation.
side_b_arguments: Under General Assembly restrictions on municipal annexation, Durham will lose the opportunity to annex the property later if it grants utilities without annexing now.
Maintaining city tax/jurisdiction parity for properties receiving city water and sewer protects long-term municipal fiscal integrity.
disagreements.resolution: Annexation and UEA passed 7-0, while the companion UDO zoning conversion to City jurisdiction passed 6-1 with Chelsea Cook voting No.

meetings.title: Durham City Council Work Session April 10, 2025
meetings.executive_summary: At the April 10, 2025 Work Session, the Durham City Council approved an excused absence for Council Member DeDreana Freeman (6-0) and discussed aligning municipal elections with even-numbered years to reduce nearly $900,000 in off-year election costs and improve turnout, referring the question to the Procedures Committee. Council also reviewed pulled consent items concerning Durham Workers' Rights Commission appointments, Chapter 70 code amendments allowing water and sewer connections within 500 feet without mandatory annexation, and a $10-year forgivable loan commitment for the Trails at Twin Lakes affordable housing project before settling the April 21 meeting agenda (6-0).

agenda_items.title: State of the City, Youth Summit, and Municipal Election Alignment Discussion
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Mayor Leonardo Williams reported on community events and the upcoming Youth Summit with Durham Public Schools before Council Member Javiera Caballero and Mayor Williams raised the prospect of shifting Durham's off-year municipal elections to even-numbered years. Speakers noted off-year municipal elections cost taxpayers nearly $900,000 while drawing low turnout, and Mayor Williams proposed referring the charter-change exploration to the Procedures Committee (chaired by Caballero), with Council Member Nate Baker adding a request to also review ward versus at-large representation.
agenda_items.vote_summary: Informational / Referred to Procedures Committee without formal vote

agenda_items.title: Excused Absence Request for Council Member DeDreana Freeman
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Mayor Leonardo Williams noted that Council Member DeDreana Freeman requested to be excused from the April 10, 2025 Work Session. Council took a voice vote to grant the excused absence.

agenda_items.title: Board, Committee, and Commission Nominations
agenda_items.discussion_summary: City Clerk staff presented ballots and nominations for upcoming board and commission appointments, including the Participatory Budgeting Steering Committee, the Mayor's Hispanic/Latino Committee, and the Durham Workers' Rights Commission. Council members submitted ballot selections ahead of formal confirmation at the regular council meeting.

agenda_items.title: Durham Workers' Rights Commission Appointments and Board Efficacy Review
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Council Member Chelsea Cook pulled Item 3 to flag a spelling correction for nominee Nina Martin and raise concern that the Durham Workers' Rights Commission had not met for three months. Council Member Carl Rist noted that DeDreana Freeman had stepped down as liaison and that he attended the commission's meeting, while Cook announced plans to review attendance, bylaws, and efficacy across all 29 City boards and commissions.

agenda_items.title: Chapter 70 City Code Amendment: Extraterritorial Water and Sewer Connections
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Council Member Nate Baker pulled Item 5 regarding Chapter 70 utility code changes that allow certain residential properties within 500 feet of an existing water or sewer main to connect without mandatory annexation into city limits. Staff confirmed that properties connecting outside corporate limits remain subject to double water and sewer rates and engineering capacity requirements.

agenda_items.title: Trails at Twin Lakes Development Loan Commitment
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Council Member Chelsea Cook pulled Item 7 to clarify terms of the City loan for the Trails at Twin Lakes affordable housing development. Community Development Director Reginald J. Johnson explained the commitment is a 10-year forgivable loan funded through the Dedicated Housing Fund to support 68 affordable units.

agenda_items.title: Settle Agenda for April 21, 2025 Regular City Council Meeting
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Deputy City Manager presented the proposed agenda configuration consisting of Consent Agenda Items 1 through 17 and General Business Agenda public hearing Items 18 through 23. Council voted unanimously among members present to settle the agenda.

votes.item_title: Excuse Absence of Council Member DeDreana Freeman from April 10, 2025 Work Session
votes.notes: DeDreana Freeman absent (excused).
votes.discussion_detail: During the opening announcements and roll call period, Mayor Leonardo Williams informed colleagues that Council Member DeDreana Freeman had requested an excused absence for the April 10, 2025 Work Session. No objections or questions were raised by the six seated members in attendance. A motion and second were heard on the floor, and Mayor Williams called for a voice vote. The motion passed unanimously 6-0 among present members, formally excusing Freeman.

meetings.title: Durham Joint City County Planning Committee (JCCPC) - April 2, 2025
meetings.executive_summary: With Vice Chair Nate Baker presiding in Chair Wendy Jacobs' absence, the Joint City County Planning Committee excused absent members, approved March 5 minutes, and voted unanimously to recommend approval of the Planning Department's FY26 Work Program focusing on three small area plans. Members held extensive policy discussions on Module 2 of the new Unified Development Ordinance (UDO), debating the elimination of minimum parking requirements, reviewing dark-sky lighting and consolidated Use Table rules, and weighing whether to retain or reform Neighborhood Protection Overlays (NPOs). Planning staff also briefed the committee on the Chapter 70 utility connection amendment heading to City Council on April 21.

agenda_items.title: Roll Call, Excused Absences, and Approval of March 5, 2025 Minutes
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Vice Chair Nate Baker called the roll with Council Member Javiera Caballero and Commissioners Chagaris, Valentine, and Burton present, and noted Chair Jacobs' absence. The committee voted unanimously to excuse Commissioner Lee and Mayor Pro Tempore Mark-Anthony Middleton and to approve the March 5, 2025 minutes.

agenda_items.title: New UDO Draft Module 2: Mobility, Parking Minimums Removal, Lighting, and Fencing
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Planning staff presented Module 2 development standards covering bicycle and pedestrian circulation, EV-capable conduit, elimination of minimum off-street parking requirements, maximum parking caps, retaining walls, and outdoor lighting with Dark Sky updates. A committee member questioned eliminating parking minimums in an auto-oriented city, while Javiera Caballero and others strongly defended removal to prevent overbuilt parking debt and align with Comprehensive Plan goals.

agenda_items.title: New UDO Use Table Continuation and Neighborhood Protection Overlays (NPOs)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Staff reviewed consolidated Use Table proposals—including 200-foot setbacks and noise studies for data centers, removing spacing restrictions for family care homes, and minor special use permits for neighborhood commercial uses in RD districts—followed by an analysis of Durham's two existing NPOs (Tuscaloosa-Lakewood and Old West Durham). Members debated whether NPOs inequitably shield organized neighborhoods from citywide density or serve as a useful anti-teardown tool if paired with clearer petition thresholds and guardrails.

agenda_items.title: Chapter 70 City Code Amendment (70-129) for Non-Annexed Utility Connections
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Planner Sarah Long presented proposed Chapter 70 amendments scheduled for City Council on April 21, allowing existing lots up to 20 acres with at most two residential units within 500 feet of an existing main—or properties with collapsed/unsatisfactory wells—to connect to water/sewer without annexation while banning extensions outside the Urban Growth Boundary. Javiera Caballero and committee members urged strict tracking to prevent tax-avoidance abuse.
agenda_items.vote_summary: Informational / Scheduled for City Council on April 21

agenda_items.title: FY26 Planning Department Work Program Recommendation
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Planning staff presented the revised FY26 Work Program reducing proposed small area plans to three in response to prior committee feedback. Javiera Caballero emphasized prioritizing quality and implementation over quantity—saying even two well-executed plans would suffice—and requested a Gantt chart timeline of long-range projects before the committee voted to recommend approval.

votes.item_title: Excuse Absence of Planning Commissioner Lee from April 2, 2025 JCCPC Meeting
votes.notes: Mark-Anthony Middleton and Commissioner Lee absent (excused); Chair Jacobs absent.
votes.discussion_detail: At the start of the April 2, 2025 JCCPC meeting, Vice Chair Nate Baker presided in the absence of Chair Wendy Jacobs and conducted roll call with City Council Member Javiera Caballero and County/Planning Commissioners Chagaris, Valentine, and Burton present. Staff noted that Commissioner Lee had requested an excused absence in advance. A motion and second to grant the excused absence were offered and passed unanimously by voice vote without discussion.

votes.item_title: Excuse Absence of Mayor Pro Tempore Mark-Anthony Middleton from April 2, 2025 JCCPC Meeting
votes.notes: Mark-Anthony Middleton requested excused absence ahead of the meeting.
votes.discussion_detail: Immediately after excusing Commissioner Lee, Vice Chair Nate Baker informed the committee that Mayor Pro Tempore Mark-Anthony Middleton had also requested an excused absence for the April 2 meeting. A motion and second were made on the floor with no opposition or abstentions. The committee approved Middleton's excused absence unanimously by voice vote.

votes.item_title: Approve Minutes of March 5, 2025 JCCPC Meeting
votes.notes: Approved March 5, 2025 committee minutes as presented.
votes.discussion_detail: Vice Chair Nate Baker introduced the draft minutes from the March 5, 2025 Joint City County Planning Committee meeting and invited any corrections or additions from members. No revisions were proposed by the City Council or County/Planning Commission representatives present. A motion and second were made and carried unanimously by voice vote.

votes.item_title: Recommend Approval of FY26 Planning Department Work Program
votes.notes: Revised work program focuses on three small area plans; Javiera Caballero requested a Gantt chart of long-range planning projects.
votes.discussion_detail: Planning staff presented the proposed FY26 Work Program as a follow-up to February's preview, noting the single substantive revision was scaling back to three small area plans rather than overloading staff capacity. Council Member Javiera Caballero commended the reduction and stressed quality over quantity—stating she would support completing two strong, implementable plans rather than rushing three—and asked for a Gantt-style visual timeline showing start and completion dates across long-range projects. No member objected to the revised scope, and Vice Chair Nate Baker called for a motion to recommend approval of the FY26 Work Program. The motion and second carried unanimously by voice vote prior to adjournment at 11:10 AM.

disagreements.meeting_title: Durham Joint City County Planning Committee (JCCPC) - April 2, 2025
disagreements.issue: Elimination of Minimum Parking Requirements in New UDO Module 2
disagreements.summary: Committee members differed over whether the new UDO should maintain complete elimination of off-street parking minimums in an auto-oriented city or monitor and revisit spillover impacts.
disagreements.side_a_position: Concerned about zero parking minimums causing street spillover and public/visitor parking burdens.
side_a_arguments: Durham remains heavily auto-dependent and visitors still drive to businesses and neighborhoods.
Without minimum parking requirements, private developments may shift parking costs and spillover burdens onto neighboring streets and the public.
disagreements.side_b_position: Strongly support permanently eliminating parking minimums to reduce housing/development costs and public parking debt.
side_b_arguments: Eliminating parking minimums was a hard-fought SCAD/UDO victory aligned with Durham's Comprehensive Plan.
Oversupplying parking created substantial debt and deficits in the City's downtown parking fund for underutilized garages.
disagreements.resolution: Staff confirmed there is no Council/County direction to restore parking minimums and that staff will monitor real-world impacts after adoption.

disagreements.meeting_title: Durham Joint City County Planning Committee (JCCPC) - April 2, 2025
disagreements.issue: Retaining Versus Eliminating Neighborhood Protection Overlays (NPOs) in New UDO
disagreements.summary: Members debated whether Neighborhood Protection Overlays reinforce inequitable density exclusion or can be reformed with guardrails to discourage small-home teardowns.
disagreements.side_a_position: Oppose retaining NPOs due to redundancy, lack of petition thresholds, and inequitable barriers to citywide density.
side_a_arguments: Tree preservation, yard landscaping, and driveway rules already achieved by NPOs are being embedded universally into the new RD base districts.
NPO petitions currently lack a minimum neighbor-approval percentage (like 51% or 60%) and favor wealthier, better-organized neighborhoods while pushing growth onto less-organized communities.
Restricting height (such as 31 feet in Old West Durham) conflicts with the Comprehensive Plan's push for density and 15-minute walkable neighborhoods.
disagreements.side_b_position: Open to retaining an NPO-like mechanism or local petition tool as a release valve if capped by Comprehensive Plan guardrails.
side_b_arguments: Residents need a legislative release valve to protect neighborhoods with existing small homes from mass teardown and mansionization.
Overlay rules could be constrained by statute or local guardrails so they cannot undo Comprehensive Plan density goals.
disagreements.resolution: Planning Director Bo Dobrzenski and Director Young agreed to return with a staff analysis on standardizing beneficial NPO rules citywide and putting guardrails on NPOs and private text amendments.
