Items 1 through 4 and 6 through 10 were assigned to the Consent Agenda, while Item 5 on the deer bow hunting ordinance was routed to the General Business Agenda for fuller public consideration. Council moved and seconded the motion without further amendment, approving the slate by unanimous 6-0 voice vote among the six members remaining present.

disagreements.meeting_title: Durham City Council Work Session December 19, 2024
disagreements.issue: Authority and Safety of Lifting the Administrative Pause on City Tent Distribution to Unsheltered Residents
disagreements.summary: Council members clashed over whether to direct staff during a work session to lift an administrative pause prohibiting HEART and other city staff from distributing tents while HSAC finalizes a countywide policy.
disagreements.side_a_position: Lift the administrative pause immediately so outreach workers can distribute tents during freezing rain without risking disciplinary retaliation.
side_a_arguments: Freezing rain and cold winter nights pose immediate danger to unsheltered residents before a formal HSAC policy is finished.
Staff such as HEART responders should not face write-ups or uncertainty for providing emergency shelter gear.
disagreements.side_b_position: Do not issue unagendized work-session directives or endorse tents as winter shelter in below-freezing weather; defer to formal policy channels and indoor shelter options.
side_b_arguments: Council cannot govern by ad hoc work-session fiat without an agendized item, staff cost data, or formal vote.
Tents are unsafe in sub-freezing temperatures; the City should explore indoor facilities such as vacant City real estate or Durham Public Schools gyms and align with HSAC.
disagreements.resolution: No formal vote was taken; Mayor Williams declined to suspend the rules and instructed City Manager Wanda Page, incoming Manager Bo Ferguson, Deputy Manager Keith Chadwell, and Community Safety Director Ryan Smith to develop an urgent response.

disagreements.meeting_title: Durham City Council Work Session December 19, 2024
disagreements.issue: Proposed Citywide Reductions to Deer Bow Hunting Acreage and Setback Buffers (Item 5)
disagreements.summary: Multiple council members pushed back on lowering the minimum parcel size from 5 to 2 acres and shrinking the dwelling setback from 250 to 60 feet citywide in response to Treyburn HOA requests.
disagreements.side_a_position: Approve relaxed citywide acreage and buffer limits so neighborhoods like Treyburn can manage severe deer overpopulation and tick-borne disease risk.
side_a_arguments: Treyburn has roughly 70 deer per square mile and cannot physically satisfy the 250-foot buffer requirement even on combined 5-acre parcels.
Certified bow hunters shooting downward from elevated 10-foot stands pose minimal risk and already operate safely in neighboring jurisdictions.
disagreements.side_b_position: Require stronger citywide safety data, daytime/signage restrictions, non-lethal alternatives, and consideration of neighborhood equity before weakening weapon discharge buffers.
side_b_arguments: A citywide ordinance change opens bow hunting in denser neighborhoods outside Treyburn with fewer notice protections for residents and pets.

Council lacked empirical deer-count data, exploration of sterilization options, and justification for prioritizing suburban deer culling relative to gun violence in communities like McDougald Terrace.
disagreements.resolution: Item 5 was placed on the January General Business Agenda rather than Consent for further deliberation and public hearing.

meetings.title: Durham City Council Dec 16 2024
meetings.executive_summary: The Durham City Council celebrated retiring City Manager Wanda Sims Page with a proclamation, Key to the City, and Order of the Long Leaf Pine after 37 years of local government service, alongside a 60th-anniversary proclamation for Sam Cooke's 'A Change Is Gonna Come.' Council approved the Consent Agenda (7-0), certified the November 2024 $200 million General Obligation Bond referendum, authorized $4.94 million across two contracts for 77 hybrid police patrol SUVs and vehicle upfitting (7-0 each) amid public pushback over November 12 encampment sweeps at Long Meadow Park, and approved a $1.75 million ARPA home-repair contract with Hayti Promise CDC and Rebuilding Together of the Triangle (7-0). Council also unanimously approved a $7,250 Spanish translation amendment with WSP USA Inc. after contentious debate over dropping contractor Idealisms LLC, and renamed Vivian Street to William V. 'Bill' Bell Way (7-0). Following closed session, Council voted to appoint Deputy City Manager William Bowman 'Bo' Ferguson as City Manager, triggering sharp objections from Council Members Chelsea Cook, DeDreana Freeman, and Javiera Caballero over the un-agendized motion, rushed vote during which Cook stated she did not cast a vote, and lack of an open national search.

agenda_items.title: Proclamation: 60th Anniversary of Sam Cooke's 'A Change Is Gonna Come'
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Mayor Pro Tempore Mark-Anthony Middleton read a proclamation honoring the 60th anniversary of Sam Cooke's 'A Change Is Gonna Come,' highlighting Cooke's May 1963 visit to Durham and interaction with North Carolina Central University sit-in activists prior to writing the song. Guests Andrea Lee, Nikia Davis, Levi Wiggins, Ruth Montia, Jason Perlmutter, and Ian Mance joined Council for remarks.

agenda_items.title: Retirement Proclamation, Key to the City, and Order of the Long Leaf Pine for City Manager Wanda Sims Page
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Mayor Leonardo Williams presented retiring City Manager Wanda Sims Page with a proclamation, the Key to the City, and North Carolina's Order of the Long Leaf Pine recognizing her 37 years of local government service and four-year tenure leading Durham through $200 million in voter-approved bonds and post-pandemic growth. Council members, the City Clerk, and City Attorney Kimberly Rehberg praised her steady leadership before Page thanked employees and residents ahead of her December 31, 2024 retirement.

agenda_items.title: Consent Agenda (Excluding Items 4, 5, 6, 10, and 14; Item 19 GBA; Item 21 Public Hearing)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Council pulled Items 4, 5, 6, 10, and 14 for comment or separate action while noting General Business Agenda Item 19 and Public Hearing Item 21. Council Member Chelsea Cook and Mayor Leonardo Williams offered brief supportive remarks on Item 10 (Durham Symphony funding) before Council adopted the remaining Consent Agenda.

agenda_items.title: GBA: First Amendment to Supplemental Agreement #3 with WSP USA Inc. (Durham Freeway Study Translation)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Council considered a $7,250 contract amendment (bringing the total contract to $438,500) for WSP USA Inc. to translate Durham Freeway Study reports into Spanish after Item 18 with Idealisms LLC was referred back. Council Member DeDreana Freeman opposed relying on internal staff instead of community-based engagement practitioners, arguing it undermined relationships built by Idealisms LLC, while Council Member Carl Rist, City Attorney Kimberly Rehberg, and others countered that municipal consultant work product belongs to the City and translating existing reports improves bilingual access.

agenda_items.title: Certification of November 5, 2024 $200 Million General Obligation Bond Referendum Results
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Council opened Item 4 to certify the November 2024 $200 million GO bond election results for streets, sidewalks, and parks. Four public commenters—Virginia Workman, Ripley Thornton, Samuel Scarboro, and Thomas Crowell-Albritton—protested the November 12 Durham Police Department sweep of the Long Meadow Park homeless encampment and urged Council to expand supportive housing, storage, and winter warming shelters before Mayor Williams opened the vote and proceeded to Item 5.

agenda_items.title: Contract with Clinton Automotive LLC dba Deacon Jones Ford for 77 Hybrid Police Patrol SUVs ($3,662,325.59)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Council considered a $3,662,325.59 fleet contract with Clinton Automotive LLC dba Deacon Jones Ford to purchase 77 hybrid police patrol SUVs. Public speaker Samuel Scarboro opposed police fleet expansion and called for redirecting funds toward housing and eviction prevention prior to Council's unanimous approval.

agenda_items.title: Contract with Dana Safety Supply Inc. for Upfitting 77 Police Patrol Vehicles ($1,274,306)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Council considered a $1,274,306 upfitting contract with Dana Safety Supply Inc. for the 77 patrol SUVs. Speaker Elizabeth Avant criticized spending nearly $5 million total on police vehicles amid homelessness and utility needs; Mayor Williams defended Durham's investments including the $95 million housing bond, ~$4 million in homeless response grants, and Legal Aid eviction funding while citing state preemptions, and Council Member Freeman challenged critics to identify specific $3.7 million budget offsets before voting unanimously to approve.

agenda_items.title: ARPA Contract with Hayti Promise CDC and Rebuilding Together of the Triangle ($1,750,000)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Council reviewed a $1,750,000 ARPA-funded home repair and neighborhood preservation contract along the Fayetteville Street Corridor. Speaker Victoria Peterson urged upgrades for the W.D. Hill Recreation Center, while City Manager Page and Interim Neighborhood Improvement Services Director Alexis John clarified upfront nonprofit disbursement rules and confirmed more than 20 vacant properties had active code-enforcement cases before Council approved the contract.

agenda_items.title: Public Hearing SN2400001: Street Renaming from Vivian Street to William V. 'Bill' Bell Way
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Council held a public hearing on street-renaming request SN2400001 honoring former Durham Mayor William V. 'Bill' Bell along Vivian Street at a signage cost of $365. Kristen Adair, Bell's daughter, thanked Council on behalf of her family before Council unanimously adopted the renaming.

agenda_items.title: Appointment of William Bowman 'Bo' Ferguson as City Manager
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Returning from closed session, Council moved to appoint Deputy City Manager William Bowman 'Bo' Ferguson as Durham's next City Manager following Wanda Page's retirement. Mayor Williams declared the vote unanimous at 02:34:12, prompting immediate objection from Council Member Chelsea Cook that she had her hand raised, believed discussion was still underway, and never cast a vote, followed by criticism from Cook, DeDreana Freeman, and Javiera Caballero regarding closed-door decision-making, omission of a public search, and procedural haste.
agenda_items.vote_summary: Passed (declared unanimous; Cook stated she did not vote)

votes.item_title: Item 19: First Amendment to Supplemental Agreement #3 with WSP USA Inc. ($7,250 Spanish Translation)
votes.notes: Brings total WSP Supplemental Agreement #3 contract to $438,500.
votes.discussion_detail: After debate between Freeman and other council members/City Attorney over consultant relationship ownership following Idealisms LLC's removal from Item 18, all seven members voted to translate the existing WSP reports into Spanish.

votes.item_title: Item 4: Certification of November 5, 2024 $200M General Obligation Bond Referendum Results
votes.notes: Numerical tally and individual member votes were not announced aloud before advancing to Item 5.
votes.discussion_detail: Public speakers criticized homeless encampment sweeps at Long Meadow Park while speaking on Item 4; Mayor Williams opened the vote at 01:46:24 and moved directly to Item 5 at 01:46:44.

votes.item_title: Item 5: Contract with Clinton Automotive LLC dba Deacon Jones Ford (77 Hybrid Police SUVs, $3,662,325.59)
votes.notes: Motion called at 01:49:09 and carried unanimously at 01:49:45.
votes.discussion_detail: Approved after public comment from Samuel Scarboro opposing police vehicle spending.

votes.item_title: Item 6: Contract with Dana Safety Supply Inc. (Upfitting 77 Police Vehicles, $1,274,306)
votes.notes: Motion called at 02:00:05 and passed unanimously at 02:02:03.
votes.discussion_detail: Approved unanimously after public comment questioning nearly $5M in total police vehicle costs and Council responses detailing Durham's affordable housing and homelessness spending.

votes.item_title: Item 14: ARPA Contract with Hayti Promise CDC & Rebuilding Together of the Triangle ($1,750,000)
votes.notes: Mayor announced 7-0 passage at 02:23:02.
votes.discussion_detail: Approved after staff clarified upfront CDC disbursement mechanics and code enforcement on vacant properties along Fayetteville Street.

votes.item_title: Item 21: Street Renaming SN2400001 (Vivian Street to William V. 'Bill' Bell Way)
votes.notes: Motion made at 02:32:06 and carried unanimously at 02:32:27.
votes.discussion_detail: Public hearing held with remarks from former Mayor Bell's daughter Kristen Adair; passed unanimously.

votes.item_title: Appointment of William Bowman 'Bo' Ferguson as City Manager
votes.tally: Declared unanimous (Cook stated she did not vote)
votes.notes: Individual roll-call votes were not read aloud; Cook's non-vote and dissent on process were entered on the record.
votes.discussion_detail: Motion made immediately after closed session without prior public agenda notice. Mayor Williams declared passage unanimous at 02:34:12, though Council Member Chelsea Cook objected at 02:34:54 and 02:45:27 that she had her hand raised to continue debate and did not vote (noting she would have voted yes had discussion proceeded properly).

disagreements.meeting_title: Durham City Council Dec 16 2024
disagreements.issue: Community Engagement Consultant Transition and Intellectual Property (Item 19 - WSP USA Translation)
disagreements.summary: Council Member DeDreana Freeman challenged relying on City staff and WSP USA Inc. after removing Idealisms LLC (Item 18), arguing it unfairly appropriated relationships built by community practitioners; other members and the City Attorney countered that municipal consultant work product belongs to the City and Spanish translation should proceed.
disagreements.side_a_position: Concerned that cutting Idealisms LLC while continuing staff-led engagement exploits community-based practitioners' relationships
side_a_arguments: Community engagement firms build years of local trust that City staff should not bypass or repurpose
Questioned continuing the study scope without the originally partnered community engagement firm
disagreements.side_b_position: Support approving the $7,250 WSP amendment to translate already-completed Durham Freeway Study reports into Spanish
side_b_arguments: City Attorney Kimberly Rehberg advised that deliverables produced under City contracts are work for hire owned by the City
Spanish-speaking residents need immediate translated access to existing technical reports
disagreements.resolution: Passed 7-0 after Council Member Freeman voted Aye while maintaining her process critique on the record.

disagreements.meeting_title: Durham City Council Dec 16 2024
disagreements.issue: City Manager Appointment Process, Transparency, and Vote Timing (Bo Ferguson)
disagreements.summary: Following a closed session, a surprise open-session motion to appoint Deputy City Manager Bo Ferguson was declared unanimously passed, sparking sharp disagreement over procedural fairness, lack of an open national search, closed-session division, and Chelsea Cook not having a chance to cast her vote.
disagreements.side_a_position: Objected to the un-agendized motion, rushed vote without discussion, and closed-door hiring process lacking a public search
side_a_arguments: Cook stated she had her hand raised to speak, did not know a final vote was closing, and never cast a ballot
Freeman cited prior closed-session disagreement (4-3 or 5-2) and criticized skipping an open search for Durham's highest-paid executive
Caballero emphasized public transparency expectations for major executive appointments and voicemail/communication delays
disagreements.side_b_position: Defended appointing internal Deputy City Manager Bo Ferguson through the same council appointment mechanism used previously
side_b_arguments: Williams and Middleton highlighted Ferguson's institutional continuity and leadership during major crises such as the 2019 gas explosion
Asserted the appointment followed the same precedent used to appoint outgoing City Manager Wanda Page
disagreements.resolution: Appointment stood as declared at 02:34:12 without a revote; Cook stated for the record she did not vote during the tally though she supported Ferguson personally.

meetings.title: Durham City Council Work Session Dec 5, 2024
meetings.executive_summary: With Mayor Leonardo Williams absent on City business in Wilmington, Mayor Pro Tempore Mark-Anthony Middleton chaired the December 5, 2024 Work Session where Council accepted City Manager Priority Items (6-0), removing Idealisms LLC (Item 18) back to Transportation and canceling Item 22. During review of pulled consent items for the December 16 regular meeting, Council Members Carl Rist, Javiera Caballero, DeDreana Freeman, and Chelsea Cook successfully polled to refer Item 13 (FY24-25 Pay Plan Amendment for ~196 bypassed Fire and Police employees) back to staff to recalculate retroactive implementation to July 1, 2024 rather than January 11, 2025. Council also heard public protest from Thomas Crowell-Albritton over the November 12 Long Meadow Park homeless encampment sweeps during discussion of Item 4 ($200M GO Bond certification), scrutinized a $1.4 million rock-excavation cost overrun on Duke/MCNC fiber construction (Item 16) and transit capital plans including a $200,000 BRT feasibility study (Item 20), and voted 6-0 to settle the December 16 agenda without Item 13.

agenda_items.title: City Manager Priority Items and Board/Commission Nominations
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Staff presented Priority Items referring Item 18 (Idealisms LLC Durham Freeway engagement) back to the Transportation Department, canceling Item 22 (Jacobs Engineering contract), and adding Item 23 (Chapman transportation response). The City Clerk also read nominations for Hispanic/Latino affairs and Planning Commission appointments before Council accepted Priority Items.

agenda_items.title: GO Bond Referendum Certification ($200M) and 77 Hybrid Police SUVs ($3.66M)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: During discussion of Item 4 certifying the $200 million GO bond vote, resident Thomas Crowell-Albritton protested the November 12 DPD sweeps at Long Meadow Park and criticized City surplus spending versus homelessness aid. On Item 5, staff member Michael Boyd answered Council Member Nate Baker's questions regarding the 77 hybrid patrol SUV purchase.

agenda_items.title: FY24-25 Pay Plan Amendment for Bypassed Public Safety Employees (~196 Fire & Police Staff)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Staff proposed a pay-plan correction costing $95,000 for the remainder of FY25 ($188,000 annualized) effective January 11, 2025 to address compression affecting roughly 196 Fire and Police employees bypassed during prior adjustments. Council Members Carl Rist, Javiera Caballero, DeDreana Freeman, and Chelsea Cook objected to delaying parity until January despite City Manager Wanda Page citing tight sales tax growth and complex overtime recalculations, leading Middleton to poll four-plus hands to refer Item 13 back to staff for a July 1, 2024 retroactive calculation.
agenda_items.vote_summary: Referred back to staff (excluded from Dec 16 agenda)

agenda_items.title: Hayti Promise ARPA Contract ($1.75M), Duke/MCNC Fiber Overrun ($1.4M), WSP Translation ($7,250), and Transit CIP
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Council reviewed Hayti Promise CDC's $1.75 million ARPA corridor repair contract (Item 14), questioned a $1.4 million subsurface rock cost overrun on the Duke/MCNC dark-fiber project (Item 16), moved WSP USA's $7,250 Spanish translation amendment (Item 19) to GBA for final decision, and examined Item 20's Transit Capital Improvement Program updates covering GoDurham Access paratransit facilities and a $200,000 Bus Rapid Transit (BRT) feasibility study.

agenda_items.title: Proposed Urban Bow Hunting Ordinance Scheduling
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Council Member Carl Rist and Mayor Pro Tempore Mark-Anthony Middleton confirmed that a revised draft of the urban bow hunting ordinance would be scheduled for further review at the December 19, 2024 work session before advancing to a regular council vote.

agenda_items.title: Settle Agenda for December 16, 2024 Regular City Council Meeting
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Council settled the December 16, 2024 agenda placing Items 1–12, 14–17, and 20 on Consent, Item 19 on General Business Agenda, and Item 21 under Public Hearings while omitting Item 13 pending staff recalculation.

votes.item_title: Accept City Manager Priority Items (Referring Item 18 to Transportation, Canceling Item 22, Adding Item 23)
votes.notes: Mayor Leonardo Williams was absent (in Wilmington).
votes.discussion_detail: Accepted priority agenda adjustments ahead of pulled-item review.

disagreements.meeting_title: Durham City Council Work Session Dec 5, 2024
disagreements.issue: Retroactive Effective Date for FY24-25 Public Safety Pay Plan Correction (Item 13)
disagreements.summary: Council debated whether pay-compression adjustments for roughly 196 bypassed Fire and Police employees should take effect January 11, 2025 as proposed by staff or retroactively to the start of the fiscal year on July 1, 2024.
disagreements.side_a_position: Make the public safety pay correction retroactive to July 1, 2024
side_a_arguments: Affected Fire and Police employees missed parity increases implemented in the FY25 budget at the start of the fiscal year
Delaying implementation until January 11, 2025 shortchanges employees who were bypassed by administrative structure
disagreements.side_b_position: Staff cautioned against mid-year retroactivity due to budget tightness and payroll calculation complexity
side_b_arguments: City Manager Wanda Page cited sluggish sales tax revenue growth (~13 months into tighter post-ARPA budgeting)
Retroactively recalculating 6 months of variable public safety overtime shifts poses heavy payroll and financial uncertainty
disagreements.resolution: Mayor Pro Tempore Middleton polled at least four supporting members and referred Item 13 back to staff to recalculate costs effective July 1, 2024; Item 13 was omitted from the December 16 agenda.

meetings.title: Durham Joint City County Planning Committee (JCCPC) - December 4, 2024
meetings.executive_summary: Chair Javiera Caballero convened the December 4, 2024 Joint City County Planning Committee (JCCPC) alongside City Council Members Nate Baker and Mark-Anthony Middleton and County Commissioners, approving the October 2, 2024 minutes unanimously by voice vote. Committee members reviewed the Walltown and Northgate Mall Small Area Plan, emphasizing targets for 20 percent affordable housing (with half serving 30–50% AMI, including a 72-unit senior housing proposal among ~140 total units) and neighborhood park and drainage improvements. Staff also presented proposed Unified Development Ordinance (UDO) Use Table restructuring designed to curb quasi-judicial Special Use Permits, simplify zoning districts, and support '15-minute city' neighborhood services, followed by a 2055 Metropolitan Transportation Plan update from Matt Day projecting 1.5 million additional regional residents and roughly 60,000 needed housing units in Durham.

agenda_items.title: Approval of October 2, 2024 JCCPC Meeting Minutes
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chair Javiera Caballero called for approval of the October 2, 2024 JCCPC meeting minutes after confirming City and County committee attendance. Present committee members approved the minutes unanimously by voice vote.

agenda_items.title: Walltown / Northgate Mall Small Area Plan Update
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Planning staff briefed JCCPC on community-informed policy drafts for the Walltown and former Northgate Mall site, highlighting targets of 20% affordable housing (half at 30–50% AMI, anchored by a 72-unit senior project toward ~140 affordable units), greenspace, drainage remediation, and transit integration. Members discussed balancing community expectations with redevelopment feasibility and advisory plan limits.

agenda_items.title: UDO Rewrite: Use Table Restructuring and Special Use Permit (SUP) Reform
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Staff outlined proposed restructuring of the Unified Development Ordinance Use Table to consolidate fragmented use categories, sharply limit quasi-judicial Special Use Permits in favor of clear by-right and design standards, adjust family care home spacing rules, and foster walkable '15-minute city' neighborhood retail.

agenda_items.title: 2055 Metropolitan Transportation Plan (MTP) Growth Projections
agenda_items.discussion_summary: MPO Director Matt Day presented long-range 2055 MTP demographic and transportation forecasts showing an additional 1.5 million residents across the Triangle region and roughly 60,000 new housing units needed in Durham, underscoring transit corridor prioritization and multi-modal investment.

votes.item_title: Approval of October 2, 2024 JCCPC Meeting Minutes
votes.notes: Only City Council JCCPC appointees from the seated City roster are listed in ayes; County Commissioners also participated as joint committee members.
votes.discussion_detail: Approved without objection by present JCCPC City Council and County Commissioner members.

meetings.title: Durham City Council Dec 2 2024
meetings.executive_summary: The December 2, 2024 Regular City Council meeting resulted in nine unanimous 7-0 votes, including a $1,000,000 ARPA award for the Fayetteville Street Corridor initiative, two rezonings, a five-year statutory vested rights extension for Davis Park Pod G, and a Victory Lane cul-de-sac closure. Council probed the Vivo Living Ivy Creek adaptive hotel reuse project closely over mold remediation, affordable voucher access, and pedestrian connectivity to MLK Parkway before approving its 128 apartments with 25 income-restricted units.

agenda_items.title: World AIDS Day Proclamation and HOPWA Grant Criticism
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chelsea Cook read the World AIDS Day proclamation recognizing December 1, 2024. Coalition representative Dr. Haley Cunningham thanked the City while criticizing the denial of a support letter for a $2.5M federal HOPWA HINT grant and unspent HOPWA allocations.

agenda_items.title: Excused Absence for Mayor Leonardo Williams (December 5 Work Session)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Council considered and unanimously approved Mayor Leonardo Williams's excused absence request for the upcoming December 5, 2024 work session.

agenda_items.title: Adoption of Consent Agenda (Items 1, 3, 5, 7-19, 21-26, 32)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Council adopted the consent docket excluding Item 6 (pulled as a resource/ARPA item), Item 20 (referred back), and Public Hearing Items 28-31.

agenda_items.title: ARPA Fayetteville Street Corridor Planning and Infrastructure Community Assistance Initiative
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Council voted separately on the pulled ARPA grant of up to $1,000,000 with Fayetteville Street Planning Group Inc. and United Way of the Greater Triangle.

agenda_items.title: Vivo Living Ivy Creek UDO Zoning Map Amendment (1920 Ivy Creek Blvd)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Public hearing on rezoning 3.59 acres from CG(D) and OI(D) to PDR 35.654 to convert a former hotel into 128 studio and one-bedroom apartments, with 25 units (20%) committed at 60% AMI for 30 years plus $10,000 each to the Affordable Housing Fund and DPS.

agenda_items.title: Hillsboro Road Commercial / Chapel Hill Tire Rezoning (2504 Hillsboro Rd)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Public hearing to rezone 0.50 acres from CD-S2 to CI(D) to expand an existing Chapel Hill Tire facility from 6 to 8 service bays, accompanied by five text commitments including Rose Hill sidewalk construction and a Hillsboro Road bus shelter (Planning Commission recommended approval 6-3).

agenda_items.title: Statutory Vested Rights Determination - Davis Park Pod G (1400 Maran Ave)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Public hearing presented by Patrick Byker and Lance Chernow to extend vested rights for site plan D2200108 on 2.83 acres through December 2, 2029, ahead of Page-Miami Design District code rules. Nate Baker and Carl Rist questioned density and pedestrian design tradeoffs relative to the newer district standards.

agenda_items.title: Permanent Street Closing - Portion of Victory Lane Cul-de-Sac Bulb (SC2300005)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Public hearing on permanently closing 2,899 square feet of the Victory Lane cul-de-sac bulb for the Fletcher Ridge/Phillips Valley development by D.R. Horton.

agenda_items.title: Lead Service Line Inventory Notice Reminder
agenda_items.discussion_summary: DeDreana Freeman reminded homeowners in pre-1988 properties who received federal lead-pipe inventory notices to contact Durham One Call at 919-560-1200 for inspection assistance.

votes.item_title: Excuse Mayor Leonardo Williams from December 5, 2024 Work Session
votes.notes: Electronic board vote approving Mayor Williams's December 5 absence.
votes.discussion_detail: Mayor Leonardo Williams requested an excused absence for the upcoming December 5, 2024 City Council Work Session prior to adopting the evening's consent agenda. No objections were raised by council colleagues regarding the scheduling conflict. A motion was made and seconded and passed unanimously 7-0 on the electronic board at 00:29:46.

votes.item_title: Item 6: ARPA Fayetteville Street Corridor Planning and Infrastructure Community Assistance Initiative (NTE $1,000,000)
votes.notes: Agreement with Fayetteville Street Planning Group Inc. and fiscal partner United Way of the Greater Triangle.
votes.discussion_detail: Pulled from the Consent Agenda for separate action, Item 6 authorized up to $1,000,000 in American Rescue Plan Act funding for the Fayetteville Street Corridor Planning and Infrastructure Community Assistance Initiative administered with Fayetteville Street Planning Group Inc. and United Way of the Greater Triangle. Having reviewed the revised scope after its earlier October referral back to staff, council members raised no further objections at the table. The motion passed unanimously 7-0 at 00:36:23.

votes.item_title: Item 28: Vivo Living Ivy Creek UDO Zoning Map Amendment (CG(D)/OI(D) to PDR 35.654, 1920 Ivy Creek Blvd)
votes.notes: Adaptive hotel reuse into 128 apartments with 25 units (20%) at 60% AMI for 30 years, $10k Housing Fund, $10k DPS, and a 12-ft shared-use path connection.
votes.discussion_detail: Planning staff presented the 3.59-acre adaptive reuse proposal by Vivo Living to convert the vacant hotel at 1920 Ivy Creek Boulevard into 128 efficiency and one-bedroom apartments with 25 affordable units at 60% AMI for 30 years. Council members probed the developer intensively: Chelsea Cook challenged an inaccuracy in the staff report listing the site as vacant and questioned mold remediation, reduced application fees, and Durham Housing Authority voucher acceptance; Nate Baker pressed on Planning Commission concerns and written fee commitments; Carl Rist secured focus on a 12-foot shared-use path to MLK Parkway; Mark-Anthony Middleton stressed parity between affordable and market units and inspection rigor; and DeDreana Freeman questioned mold inspection methods. Satisfied with the applicant's proffers and commitments, Council approved the rezoning unanimously 7-0 at 01:19:04.

votes.item_title: Item 28: Consistency Statement under NCGS 160D-605 (Vivo Living Ivy Creek)
votes.notes: Statutory consistency finding with the Comprehensive Plan.
votes.discussion_detail: Immediately following approval of the Vivo Living Ivy Creek zoning map amendment, Council considered the mandatory statutory consistency statement pursuant to NCGS 160D-605. The statement affirmed that the PDR 35.654 adaptive-reuse residential project aligns with the Comprehensive Plan's goals for infill housing and transit-accessible affordability. Council adopted the consistency statement 7-0 at 01:19:38.

votes.item_title: Item 29: Hillsboro Road Commercial / Chapel Hill Tire UDO Zoning Map Amendment (CD-S2 to CI(D), 2504 Hillsboro Rd)
votes.notes: Allows expansion from 6 to 8 service bays with 5 text commitments including Rose Hill sidewalk and a Hillsboro Rd bus shelter; Planning Commission voted 6-3 in favor.
votes.discussion_detail: Staff and representatives for Chapel Hill Tire presented the 0.50-acre rezoning from CD-S2 to Commercial Infill with Development Plan (CI(D)) to expand from six to eight automotive service bays at 2504 Hillsboro Road, noting the Planning Commission's 6-3 recommendation of approval. Speakers and council members examined neighborhood pedestrian safety along Rose Hill Avenue, noise/hours buffers, and how the five text commitments address stormwater and a Hillsboro Road transit shelter. Council members commended the transit and sidewalk investments on an older suburban commercial parcel and approved the rezoning unanimously 7-0 at 01:48:46.

votes.item_title: Item 29: Consistency Statement under NCGS 160D-605 (Hillsboro Road Commercial)
votes.discussion_detail: Following the Hillsboro Road Commercial rezoning approval, Council voted on the companion NCGS 160D-605 consistency statement. Council affirmed that the CI(D) expansion with committed sidewalk and bus-shelter improvements was consistent and reasonable under the Comprehensive Plan. The motion passed unanimously 7-0 at 01:49:14.

votes.item_title: Item 30: Ordinance Approving Statutory Vested Rights Determination for Davis Park Pod G (1400 Maran Ave)

meetings.title: Durham City Council Work Session Nov 21, 2024
meetings.executive_summary: At the November 21, 2024 Work Session, Council suspended the rules to pass an NCDOT-required resolution closing streets for the December Durham Holiday Parade and reviewed the clean FY24 Annual Comprehensive Financial Report alongside the FY25 Q1 financial update. Police Chief Patrice Andrews delivered the Q3 2024 crime report amid council questions on stolen guns, ShotSpotter, police staffing at 73%, and U-Visas, followed by a split in tone as Council reluctantly voted 7-0 to enter closed session on a personnel matter.

agenda_items.title: City Manager Priority Items, Rules Suspension & Item 20 Holiday Parade Street Closures
agenda_items.discussion_summary: City Manager Wanda Page introduced priority additions including the ACFR presentation (Item 4), referral back of Item 13, Q3 crime report (Item 21), supplemental Sandy Ridge Villas loan assignment (Item 32), and immediate action on Item 20 for 2024 Holiday Parade NCDOT street closures.
agenda_items.vote_summary: Priority items, rules suspension, and Item 20 all approved 7-0

agenda_items.discussion_summary: District Attorney Satana Deberry and Community Safety Director Ryan Smith answered council questions on renewed city funding supporting domestic violence prosecution and gang-reduction coordination.

agenda_items.title: Q3 2024 Durham Police Department Crime Report
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Police Chief Patrice Andrews and Deputy Chief Walter Tate presented Q3 crime statistics, prompting council inquiries on stolen firearms from unlocked cars, federal Tiahrt Amendment restrictions, ShotSpotter outcomes, sworn staffing levels (73%), and U-Visa certifications.

agenda_items.title: Closed Session under NCGS 143-318.11(a)(6) (Personnel) & Lead Pipe Notice Discussion
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Council voted 7-0 to enter closed session for personnel matters, though Cook and Freeman objected to handling major leadership-transition discussions without broader public engagement. Afterward at 02:19:51, Freeman raised resident confusion over pre-1988 lead service line letters.
agenda_items.vote_summary: Closed Session approved 7-0; Set Agenda approved 7-0

votes.item_title: Accept City Manager's Priority Items
votes.notes: Nate Baker arrived during council announcements at 00:03:21 prior to all votes.
votes.discussion_detail: City Manager Wanda Page presented her priority updates for the November 21 work session, including moving the ACFR presentation (Item 4), referring Item 13 back to staff, presenting the Q3 Crime Report (Item 21), requesting immediate action on Holiday Parade street closures (Item 20), and adding supplemental Item 32 for Sandy Ridge Villas. Council had no objections to incorporating these priority adjustments into the afternoon's schedule. A motion to accept the priority items was moved, seconded, and approved 7-0 by voice vote.

votes.item_title: Suspend the Rules to Vote on Item 20 (Durham Holiday Parade Street Closures)
votes.notes: Required to take final action during a Work Session due to new NCDOT timing requirements.
votes.discussion_detail: Because new North Carolina Department of Transportation permitting requirements required formal Council approval before the December regular meeting in order for the annual Durham Holiday Parade to proceed on state-maintained downtown roadways, the administration asked Council to suspend its work-session rules. No council member opposed expediting the procedural authorization given the upcoming event date. Council moved, seconded, and unanimously passed the rules suspension 7-0 by voice vote.

votes.item_title: Item 20: Resolution Approving Street Closures for the 2024 Durham Holiday Parade
votes.notes: Satisfies NCDOT requirement for temporary state-roadway closures.
votes.discussion_detail: Immediately following the rules suspension, Mayor Leonardo Williams entertained a motion to adopt the resolution authorizing temporary street closures for the 2024 Durham Holiday Parade. Staff noted that NCDOT newly required an explicit governing-body resolution ahead of the parade date rather than standard administrative permitting alone. Council expressed support for keeping the community tradition on schedule and passed the resolution unanimously 7-0 by voice vote at 00:14:00.

votes.item_title: Motion to Enter Closed Session under NCGS 143-318.11(a)(6) (Personnel)
votes.notes: Chelsea Cook and DeDreana Freeman voted Aye reluctantly while objecting to insufficient public/stakeholder process.
votes.discussion_detail: Council considered a motion to enter closed session pursuant to NCGS 143-318.11(a)(6) for confidential personnel deliberations ahead of City Manager Wanda Page's upcoming retirement. Before voting, Chelsea Cook and DeDreana Freeman voiced frustration that sensitive decisions surrounding top leadership and interim planning were being handled privately without public or stakeholder engagement. Mayor Pro Tem Mark-Anthony Middleton defended closed-session confidentiality as standard and legally necessary for personnel matters. After registering those objections on the record, Council approved entering closed session 7-0 at 02:19:19.

votes.item_title: Set the Agenda for Next Regular City Council Meeting (Consent: 1, 3-12, 14-19, 21-26, 32; GBA Public Hearings: 28-31)
votes.notes: Item 13 referred back; Item 20 already acted upon.
votes.discussion_detail: Prior to convening in closed session, City Manager Wanda Page read the recommended agenda placement for the December 2, 2024 regular Council meeting, assigning Items 1, 3 through 12, 14 through 19, 21 through 26, and supplemental Item 32 to the Consent Agenda while placing Items 28 through 31 on the General Business Public Hearings docket. Item 13 remained referred back to Engineering and Infrastructure, and Item 20 had already been resolved at the work session. Council moved, seconded, and unanimously adopted the schedule 7-0 by voice vote at 02:25:39.

disagreements.meeting_title: Durham City Council Work Session Nov 21, 2024
disagreements.issue: Public and Stakeholder Transparency in Executive Personnel Discussions (Closed Session NCGS 143-318.11(a)(6))
disagreements.summary: Although all seven members voted to enter closed session, members disagreed sharply on whether executive transition deliberations were overly shielded from community input.
disagreements.side_a_position: Executive transition and key leadership-role discussions require structured public and stakeholder engagement rather than being handled primarily behind closed doors.
side_a_arguments: Major community-facing leadership roles affect residents directly and merit public input on priorities and expectations.
Supporting the statutory closed-session vote should not be mistaken for endorsing a closed-off transition process.
disagreements.side_b_position: Personnel evaluations, candidate discussions, and contractual deliberations must remain confidential in closed session to comply with North Carolina law and protect candor.
side_b_arguments: NCGS 143-318.11(a)(6) specifically authorizes confidential personnel deliberation when evaluating individuals or terms.
disagreements.resolution: Council unanimously voted 7-0 to enter closed session at 02:19:19 after Cook and Freeman placed their process objections on the public record.

meetings.title: Durham City Council Nov 18 2024
meetings.executive_summary: At the November 18, 2024 regular meeting, all seven Council members unanimously adopted Consent Agenda Items 1–20 (7-0) and approved transitional annexation/zoning for Constitution Drive right-of-way (7-0 across three votes), the 126-unit Vivo Living hotel-conversion apartment rezoning at 4515 NC 55 including 25 units at 60% AMI (7-0), and the Caring House expansion at 2625 Pickett Road (7-0). However, Council split 4-3 on two rural-edge residential annexations and rezonings—Doc Nichols Townes (25 townhomes on Doc Nichols Road) and Tri Creek (6017–6023 Leesville Road)—with Mayor Williams, Mayor Pro Tempore Middleton, and Council Members Caballero and Rist voting Aye while Council Members Baker, Cook, and Freeman dissented over suburban sprawl, Lick/Hurricane Creek sediment and stream-buffer impacts, blasting wells, and the Davidson Rural Area Plan (though consistency statements passed 7-0). During the Doc Nichols Townes debate, Middleton clashed sharply with Baker and invoked a procedural point of order against Freeman over comments referencing developer representatives.

agenda_items.title: Consent Agenda Items 1–20
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Council reviewed and passed Consent Agenda Items 1 through 20 together without items pulled for separate floor debate.

agenda_items.title: Constitution Drive Right-of-Way Annexation and Initial Zoning (RS-20)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Council held a public hearing on Southland Associates' transitional annexation and RS-20 city zoning application for Constitution Drive right-of-way. No opposition emerged and Council unanimously passed the annexation, zoning map change, and consistency statement.

agenda_items.title: Vivo Living Durham (4515 NC 55) Zoning Map Change (OI to PDR 53.390)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Council considered rezoning 4515 NC 55 from OI to PDR 53.390 to convert an existing hotel into 126 studio/multifamily apartments, including 25 affordable units at 60% AMI plus proffers of $10,000 to Durham Public Schools and $10,000 to the Dedicated Housing Fund. Council Member Chelsea Cook questioned $150–$200 nonrefundable application fees and background screening policies before Council unanimously approved the rezoning and consistency statement.

agenda_items.title: Doc Nichols Townes (1321 Doc Nichols Rd) Annexation and Zoning Map Change (RR to PDR 5.55)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Council considered annexing and rezoning 1321 Doc Nichols Road from RR to PDR 5.55 for 25 townhomes with proffers of $10,000 to DPS, $25,000 to the Housing Fund, and a conditional 10-foot multiuse path. Surrounding residents cited traffic, Lick/Hurricane Creek sediment runoff, blasting, and reduced 30-foot stream buffers, igniting heated Council debate between supporters emphasizing housing supply and dissenters citing rural preservation and environmental protection.

agenda_items.title: Tri Creek (6017 & 6023 Leesville Rd) Annexation and Zoning Map Change (RR to PDR 3.768)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Council reviewed annexation and rezoning of 6017 and 6023 Leesville Road from RR to PDR 3.768 with proffers of $5,000 to DPS and $20,000 to the Housing Fund. Council split 4-3 along the same urban-perimeter fault lines seen on Doc Nichols Townes before adopting the consistency statement unanimously.

agenda_items.title: Caring House Expansion (2625 Pickett Rd) Zoning Map Change (PDR 0.000 Amendment)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Council held a public hearing on an amended PDR 0.000 development plan to allow expansion of the Caring House cancer-patient lodging facility at 2625 Pickett Road. Council praised the nonprofit mission and unanimously approved both the zoning change and consistency statement.

votes.discussion_detail: Passed 4-3 approving 25 townhomes at 1321 Doc Nichols Rd.

votes.discussion_detail: Adopted NCGS 160D-605 consistency statement unanimously following the 4-3 rezoning vote.

votes.discussion_detail: Passed 4-3 along the same rural-annexation coalition lines.

votes.discussion_detail: Passed 4-3.

votes.discussion_detail: Adopted statutory consistency statement unanimously.

votes.discussion_detail: Approved Caring House nonprofit cancer-patient lodging expansion.

votes.discussion_detail: Adopted statutory consistency statement unanimously.

disagreements.issue: Rural-Perimeter Annexation, Watershed Buffers, and Rural Area Plan Precedent (Item 23: Doc Nichols Townes)
disagreements.summary: Council divided 4-3 and engaged in sharp debate—including a point of order called by Middleton during Freeman's remarks—over extending municipal utilities and townhome density into the Doc Nichols Road rural periphery amid resident warnings on Lick/Hurricane Creek sediment, well blasting, and stream-buffer reductions.
disagreements.side_a_position: Approve annexation and PDR 5.55 rezoning with housing/school/trail proffers

Includes $25,000 Dedicated Housing Fund and $10,000 DPS proffers plus conditional 10-foot multiuse path
Middleton argued Baker's invocation of external Davidson Rural Area Plan standards conflicted with Durham's Comprehensive Plan framework
disagreements.side_b_position: Deny annexation and rezoning to protect watershed buffers and curb peripheral suburban sprawl
side_b_arguments: Opposed extending City sewer outside core infrastructure into rural neighborhoods lacking nearby transit or services
Cited Lick/Hurricane Creek sediment impacts, blasting impacts on neighboring wells, and loss of 30-foot stream buffers
Baker referenced regional rural-preservation tools such as the Davidson Rural Area Plan
disagreements.resolution: Annexation and zoning passed 4-3; consistency statement adopted 7-0.

meetings.title: Durham City Council Work Session Nov 7, 2024
meetings.executive_summary: Convening two days after the November 5 general election, Council celebrated Durham voters overwhelmingly passing $200 million in Parks and Streets/Sidewalks general obligation bonds (75% and 71% approval). In a concise work session with Mark-Anthony Middleton on an excused absence, Council reviewed transit center CMAR costs (~$26M), GoDurham Access property acquisition, ParkMobile payment equity for unbanked residents, and resolved a DOST appointment tie before unanimously setting the upcoming agenda 6-0.

agenda_items.title: Post-Election Reflections and Celebration of $200 Million General Obligation Bonds
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Council reflected on the November 5, 2024 election and celebrated voter passage of the $200 million Parks & Recreation and Streets & Sidewalks bond referendums by 75% and 71% margins respectively. Mark-Anthony Middleton's excused absence (attending an NCLM hurricane relief meeting in Morganton) was noted at 00:00:22.

agenda_items.title: Public Comments on Wildlife Feeding, Eviction Diversion, and East Main Safety
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Speakers requested a Treyburn wildlife-feeding ordinance to deter deer habituation (Stephen Harris), urged emergency funding for Entry Point Durham's depleted eviction diversion program and tenant protections (Grace Wakeman and Emily Wilks), and raised drug activity and safety concerns near East Main and Stokes Streets (Regina Frazier, PAC 5).

agenda_items.title: FY25-26 Budget Development Schedule and Non-Digital Outreach
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Council reviewed the upcoming FY25-26 budget calendar and stressed ensuring non-digital engagement options for residents without reliable internet access.

agenda_items.title: Durham Station Transit Center CMAR GMP Amendment and GoDurham Access Property Acquisition
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Transportation staff reviewed the Durham Station Transit Center CMAR guaranteed maximum price amendment (~$26 million total project cost) and property acquisition plans at 00:49:20 for a dedicated GoDurham Access paratransit facility.

agenda_items.title: ParkMobile Pay-by-Phone Parking Equity for Unbanked and Elderly Residents
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Council questioned ParkMobile convenience-fee structures and accessibility for unbanked, cash-reliant, and elderly downtown parkers.

agenda_items.title: Board and Commission Nominations (DOST Tie Resolution, Appearance Commission, HRC, PB Steering)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The Clerk reported nominations for Appearance Commission (Allison P. Steele, Caitlin Wheeler), Human Relations Commission (Scott Brummel, Shandra M. Jones), and Participatory Budgeting Steering Committee (Samuel F. Thomas III), while a tie on the Durham Open Space and Trails Commission (DOST) was resolved when Chelsea Cook shifted her vote from Alexis Steele to Lindsay S. Biersbach.

agenda_items.title: Set the Agenda for Next Regular City Council Meeting
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Council set the November regular meeting agenda placing Items 1-20 on Consent and Public Hearing Items 21-25 on the General Business Agenda.

votes.item_title: Set the Agenda for Next Regular City Council Meeting (Consent: Items 1-20; GBA Public Hearings: Items 21-25)
votes.notes: Mark-Anthony Middleton had an excused absence attending a North Carolina League of Municipalities hurricane relief meeting in Morganton.
votes.discussion_detail: Having reviewed the pulled budget schedule, transit capital projects, and parking items as well as resolving the DOST board nomination tie in open session, Council took up the recommended regular-meeting docket. Items 1 through 20 were placed on the Consent Agenda and public hearings 21 through 25 were assigned to the General Business Agenda. With Mark-Anthony Middleton absent on an approved excused absence, the six present council members moved, seconded, and approved the agenda unanimously 6-0 by voice vote.

meetings.title: Durham City Council Nov 4, 2024
meetings.executive_summary: In a marathon four-hour regular session on November 4, 2024, Council took 12 formal votes highlighted by two sharp 4-3 zoning splits over suburban greenfield projects opposed by the Planning Commission. Mayor Leonardo Williams, Mark-Anthony Middleton, Javiera Caballero, and Carl Rist overcame objections from Nate Baker, Chelsea Cook, and DeDreana Freeman to approve the 102-unit Lindley Townhouses rezoning (over a 10-3 Planning Commission denial) and Drees Homes' 120-unit Sharon Grove annexation and rezoning (over a 12-1 Planning Commission denial) after mid-meeting proffer increases.

agenda_items.title: Family Homelessness Awareness Week Proclamation, Hispanic Heritage Honorees, and Closed Session Report
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Council issued a proclamation for Family Homelessness Awareness Week accepted by Atasha Melvin of Families Moving Forward, read Hispanic Heritage Month honoree names (00:16:23), excused Mark-Anthony Middleton for November 7 (00:42:14), and reported out from its pre-meeting closed session on annual evaluations and salary adjustments for Clerk Diana Schreiber, City Attorney Kim Rehberg, and City Manager Wanda Page (00:49:05).

agenda_items.title: Consent Agenda Adoption (Items 1, 4-8)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Council approved routine consent items 1 and 4 through 8 while pulling Item 3 (Kunshan Sister Cities agreement) for amendment and reserving Items 11-13 for public hearings.

agenda_items.title: Sister Cities Agreement with Kunshan, China
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Council amended the draft Sister Cities agreement with Kunshan, China to strike the final 60-day termination sentence of Section 5 and then authorized Mayor Williams to sign the amended agreement.

agenda_items.title: Lindley Townhouses UDO Zoning Map Amendment (1343 Ellis Rd & 1326 Clinton Rd)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Lengthy public hearing on rezoning 12.25 acres from RR to PDR 8.326 for 102 townhomes (5% at 80% AMI for 30 years, 100-year stormwater standard, and a 10-ft path commitment added at 01:56:43). Facing a 10-3 Planning Commission denial recommendation and heavy resident opposition over Ellis Road traffic and flooding, Council split 4-3 to approve.

agenda_items.title: Sharon Grove Consolidated Annexation and Rezoning (803, 901, 903 Sharon Rd)

votes.item_title: Item 11: Lindley Townhouses UDO Zoning Map Amendment (RR to PDR 8.326, 1343 Ellis Rd & 1326 Clinton Rd)
votes.notes: Planning Commission recommended denial 10-3; developer committed 5% units at 80% AMI for 30 yrs, 100-yr stormwater standard, and a 10-ft path added during hearing.
votes.discussion_detail: Applicant representatives sought to rezone 12.25 acres from Rural Residential to Planned Development Residential 8.326 for 102 townhomes, adding a 10-foot pedestrian path proffer during the hearing alongside 5% units at 80% AMI for 30 years and 100-year stormwater detention. Nearby residents strongly opposed the project citing narrow Ellis Road access, flooding, and a 10-3 Planning Commission denial recommendation. Opponents Nate Baker, Chelsea Cook, and DeDreana Freeman argued the suburban site lacked transit, pedestrian infrastructure, and deep affordability while overriding community and Planning Commission opposition; supporters Williams, Middleton, Caballero, and Rist argued Durham urgently needs homeownership townhome supply near major job corridors and praised the stormwater and path upgrades. The rezoning narrowly passed 4-3 at 03:14:54.

votes.item_title: Item 11: Consistency Statement under NCGS 160D-605 (Lindley Townhouses)
votes.notes: Statutory consistency finding following split 4-3 zoning approval.
votes.discussion_detail: Following the contentious 4-3 vote approving the Lindley Townhouses rezoning, Council voted on the companion NCGS 160D-605 consistency statement. Even the three council members who had opposed the rezoning joined the majority on the procedural consistency finding acknowledging the Urban Growth Boundary and Place Type alignment in the adopted map. The consistency statement passed 7-0 at 03:15:24.

votes.item_title: Item 12: Sharon Grove Consolidated Annexation and Utility Extension Agreement (803, 901, 903 Sharon Rd)
votes.notes: Initially misread as 5-2 before immediately being corrected to 4-3 to include Nate Baker's Nay vote; Drees Homes increased Housing Fund proffer to $120k and DPS to $21k after a break.
votes.discussion_detail: Drees Homes sought annexation and rezoning of 24.2 acres along Sharon Road for 120 total single-family detached homes (57 additional lots on parcel 803), carrying a 12-1 Planning Commission denial recommendation and zero on-site affordable units. After a council break, the developer raised its proffers to $120,000 for the Affordable Housing Fund, $21,000 for Durham Public Schools, and 100-year stormwater detention. Baker, Cook, and Freeman objected to single-family-only greenfield expansion without walkable urban form or on-site affordability, while Williams, Middleton, Caballero, and Rist argued the site sits inside the Urban Growth Boundary, replaces worse county-jurisdiction outcomes, and delivers housing supply plus cash proffers. Council members maintained the exact positions debated during the annexation hearing regarding greenfield infrastructure costs, car-dependent single-family sprawl, and housing supply versus cash affordable-housing contributions. The zoning map amendment passed along the same 4-3 divide at 04:10:19.

votes.item_title: Item 12: Consistency Statement under NCGS 160D-605 (Sharon Grove)
votes.discussion_detail: Council next took up the statutory NCGS 160D-605 consistency statement for the Sharon Grove RS-8(D) rezoning. Consistent with Durham practice separating policy opposition from statutory Place Type findings, all seven members voted in favor of adopting the consistency statement. The vote passed 7-0 at 04:10:53.

votes.item_title: Item 13: Winsford at the Park Consolidated Annexation (103 Zante Currant Rd)
votes.notes: 1.79-acre open-space cleanup annexation.
votes.discussion_detail: Staff presented Item 13 as a technical open-space annexation cleanup covering 1.79 acres at 103 Zante Currant Road adjacent to the existing Winsford at the Park development. No residents spoke against the boundary cleanup during the public hearing. Council approved the annexation and utility extension order unanimously 7-0 at 04:14:52.

votes.item_title: Item 13: Winsford at the Park UDO Zoning Map Amendment to RS-M(D)
votes.discussion_detail: Immediately after annexing 103 Zante Currant Road, Council voted on zoning the 1.79-acre open-space parcel to Residential Suburban Multifamily with Development Plan (RS-M(D)) to match the parent development. No additional debate occurred. The zoning map amendment passed unanimously 7-0 at 04:15:17.

votes.item_title: Item 13: Consistency Statement under NCGS 160D-605 (Winsford at the Park)
votes.discussion_detail: To complete the Winsford at the Park boundary cleanup, Council considered the statutory NCGS 160D-605 consistency statement. Having confirmed the parcel merely brings open space into city jurisdiction under matching zoning, Council adopted the statement 7-0 at 04:15:44.

disagreements.meeting_title: Durham City Council Nov 4, 2024
disagreements.issue: Lindley Townhouses Suburban Greenfield Rezoning over Planning Commission 10-3 Denial (Item 11)
disagreements.summary: Council divided 4-3 over rezoning 12.25 rural residential acres on Ellis and Clinton Roads for 102 townhomes amid resident flooding/traffic objections and a 10-3 Planning Commission denial.
disagreements.side_a_position: Approve the PDR 8.326 townhome rezoning based on housing supply needs, 5% homeownership affordability, and enhanced stormwater and path commitments.
side_a_arguments: Durham urgently needs missing-middle townhomes and entry-level homeownership opportunities near jobs.
The developer added a 10-foot pedestrian path and 100-year stormwater detention exceeding baseline rules, and 5% of units at 80% AMI for 30 years provides meaningful workforce housing.
disagreements.side_b_position: Deny the rezoning in deference to the Planning Commission's 10-3 vote, neighborhood safety concerns, and inadequate transit/pedestrian context.
side_b_arguments: Ellis Road and surrounding rural roads lack sidewalks, transit, and infrastructure for higher townhome density.
Overriding a 10-3 Planning Commission denial for only 5% affordability at 80% AMI sets a weak standard for greenfield development.
disagreements.resolution: Approved 4-3 at 03:14:54.

disagreements.meeting_title: Durham City Council Nov 4, 2024
disagreements.issue: Sharon Grove Single-Family Annexation and Rezoning without On-Site Affordability (Item 12)
disagreements.summary: Council split 4-3 on annexing and rezoning 24.2 acres along Sharon Road for Drees Homes' 120-unit single-family project despite a 12-1 Planning Commission denial.
disagreements.side_a_position: Approve the annexation and RS-8(D) rezoning after Drees Homes increased cash proffers to $120,000 for housing and $21,000 for schools.
side_a_arguments: The site lies inside the Urban Growth Boundary and annexing it yields city water/sewer oversight, 100-year stormwater standards, and $141,000 in combined Housing Fund and DPS contributions.
Denying annexation leaves the property open to lower-standard county development without affordable housing proffers.
disagreements.side_b_position: Reject single-family-only suburban sprawl inside the UGB lacking mixed housing types, walkability, and on-site affordable units.
side_b_arguments: The Planning Commission overwhelmingly recommended denial 12-1.
Zero on-site affordable units and a car-oriented single-family layout run counter to Durham's Comprehensive Plan Place Type principles.
disagreements.resolution: Annexation and zoning both passed 4-3 at 04:08:35 and 04:09:41 (following correction of Baker's Nay vote).

meetings.title: Durham City Council Work Session October 24, 2024
meetings.executive_summary: The October 24, 2024 Work Session—opened by Mayor Pro Tem Mark-Anthony Middleton before Mayor Leonardo Williams arrived—centered on three policy debates without formal action: testing the Environmental Affairs Board's Sustainable Decision-Making Tool, reallocating $249,000 in unobligated ARPA funds (with Council rejecting internal salary use in favor of kindergarten baby bonds or existing youth nonprofits), and HR Director Robin Wynn's 30-day recruitment timeline for a new City Manager. Council passed five procedural votes 6-0 with DeDreana Freeman on an excused absence.

agenda_items.title: Opening Remarks, Excused Absences (Cook & Williams), and Priority Items
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Mayor Pro Tem Middleton called the meeting to order with DeDreana Freeman on an excused absence; Mayor Williams arrived at 00:06:21. Council excused Cook for November 7 and Williams for December 5, approved an attorney-client closed session, accepted priority items (referring back Item 2 Fayetteville St ARPA and adding Item 14 CM Recruitment), and moved the Clerk's B&C report to Priority Items (Mary Ellen Green nominated to BPAC).

agenda_items.title: Sister Cities Agreement with Kunshan, China
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Carl Rist asked about Durham maintaining two Sister City partnerships in China (joining Xi'an), and staff confirmed no policy bars multiple sister cities in a large nation.

agenda_items.title: Environmental Affairs Board (EAB) Sustainable Decision-Making Tool Presentation
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The EAB chair presented a standardized sustainability impact checklist for cross-departmental budget and policy decisions. Caballero, Cook, and Rist backed running a collaborative staff test case, while Mayor Williams objected to bypassing City staff and Middleton questioned extra bureaucracy.
agenda_items.vote_summary: Informational / Direction to work with staff

agenda_items.title: ARPA Update and Reallocation Options for Remaining $249,000
agenda_items.discussion_summary: DCM Bertha Johnson-Winbush and Victoria Samayoa recommended retaining $249,000 in unobligated ARPA interest/funds to cover admin salaries and software. Council members unanimously preferred community deployment before December 31, debating Mayor Williams and Carl Rist's kindergarten baby bonds concept versus existing vetted nonprofits like El Futuro, Book Harvest, or Knox Street.
agenda_items.vote_summary: Informational / Staff directed to explore options

agenda_items.title: Supplemental: City Manager Executive Recruitment Plan & Interim Planning
agenda_items.discussion_summary: HR Director Robin Wynn outlined an internal HR-led recruitment plan featuring a 30-day national posting (Nov 10-Dec 10), SharePoint screening, and Jan/Feb interviews. Cook urged assessment centers and community finalist panels, while Middleton warned the schedule leaves a post-December vacancy requiring a November 4 6:00 PM closed session on interim leadership and alternatives.

agenda_items.title: Set the Agenda for November 4 Regular City Council Meeting
agenda_items.discussion_summary: City Manager Wanda Page presented the November 4 agenda placing Item 1 and Items 3-8 on Consent and Items 11-13 on General Business Public Hearings (following staff recognition of Erin Miles winning IMLA's Young Public Lawyer Award).

votes.notes: Requested by Senior Deputy City Attorney Fred Lamar; held at the conclusion of the work session.

disagreements.meeting_title: Durham City Council Work Session October 24, 2024
disagreements.issue: Process and Utility of Testing the EAB Sustainable Decision-Making Tool (Item 9)
disagreements.summary: Council divided over advancing an Environmental Affairs Board sustainability assessment checklist directly to a Council test case versus requiring staff vetting first and limiting bureaucratic layers.
disagreements.side_a_position: Run a collaborative test case with staff to standardize sustainability and equity metrics across all City departments.
side_a_arguments: A single standardized rubric gives non-expert policymakers consistent data instead of piecemeal departmental reports.
Piloting one item with staff will quickly show whether the tool helps or burdens workflows.
disagreements.side_b_position: Require advisory boards to collaborate directly with City staff experts before asking Council to approve or pilot an operational tool.
side_b_arguments: Bypassing department staff demoralizes professional staff and creates out-of-order policy proposals.
Existing staff already incorporate sustainability and racial equity considerations without needing extra bureaucratic checklists.
disagreements.resolution: Caballero and Cook clarified the test case meant EAB working directly with appropriate staff first; no formal vote was taken.

disagreements.meeting_title: Durham City Council Work Session October 24, 2024
disagreements.issue: Deployment of Remaining $249,000 in Unobligated ARPA Funds (Item 10)
disagreements.summary: While Council rejected staff's recommendation to keep $249,000 internally for administrative salaries, members differed on whether to seed universal kindergarten baby bonds or fund existing nonprofits.
disagreements.side_a_position: Use the $249,000 as seed money—paired with corporate matches and Latino Credit Union/DPS Foundation partnerships—to launch kindergarten baby bonds / youth savings accounts.
side_a_arguments: Starting accounts (~$25 per student for ~2,000 kindergarteners born during the pandemic) creates long-term generational wealth and leverages corporate matching from firms like Wells Fargo.
Means-testing City revenue-replacement dollars complies with state law while private funds cover universal access.
disagreements.side_b_position: Prioritize already-vetted nonprofits or existing ARPA partners (such as El Futuro, Book Harvest, or Knox Street) due to extreme December 31 contracting and legal constraints.
side_b_arguments: Legal and staff capacity constraints make negotiating a brand-new subrecipient agreement and means-tested bond structure by December 31 high risk.
Existing nonprofits such as El Futuro or homelessness/food organizations already have vetted scopes ready to deploy funds without risking federal clawback.
disagreements.resolution: Council directed staff to pursue baby bonds feasibility via existing partners such as United Way/LCCCU/DPS Foundation while preparing fallback options among existing youth-serving ARPA grantees.

disagreements.meeting_title: Durham City Council Work Session October 24, 2024
disagreements.issue: City Manager Recruitment Timeline, Interview Format, and Interim Governance (Item 14)
disagreements.summary: Members agreed on HR leading the search but differed on moving straight into the proposed timeline versus pausing for closed-session deliberation over interim leadership and alternative paths.
disagreements.side_a_position: Proceed briskly with the HR-led national posting, adding virtual screening, in-person finalist visits with community/stakeholder roundtables, and assessment center exercises.
side_a_arguments: Time is tight and an aggressive 30-day holiday posting window captures qualified candidates cleanly.
Bringing at least two finalists in person and using EQI/assessment centers ensures rigorous vetting.
disagreements.side_b_position: Flag that the proposed timeline extends past December 31 without a manager, necessitating closed-session discussion of an interim manager and alternative options.
side_b_arguments: Full endorsement of the posted timeline should wait until Council holds a personnel closed session to weigh interim appointment and alternative recruitment options.
disagreements.resolution: Council agreed by consensus to hold a closed session on November 4 at 6:00 PM prior to the regular meeting while HR drafts the recruitment brochure for November 7 review.
